+import DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942ResetHorizontal
+import DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942Boundary
+
+/-!
+# Propagating one actual reset across a seam-free integer interval
+
+Color1 propagates in both horizontal directions. The exact local tile
+classification then forces a reset at each interior position. The only
+geometry input is explicit absence of seams in that interval; periodicity,
+unique Start, an assumed reset row and machine semantics are not used.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942ResetRows
+
+open WangTiles942 WangTiles942Language WangTiles942ResetHorizontal WangTiles942Boundary
+
+set_option Elab.async false
+set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000
+set_option maxRecDepth 10000
+
+/-- Exact membership in the three reset tiles, retaining the south color. -/
+def ResetTile (t : Tile) : Prop := ∃ p ∈ [434,435,436], t = ⟨1,438,1,p⟩
+
+theorem ResetTile.horizontal {t : Tile} (h : ResetTile t) : t.west = 1 ∧ t.east = 1 := by
+  obtain ⟨p,hp,rfl⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨rfl,rfl⟩
+
+theorem ResetTile.north {t : Tile} (h : ResetTile t) : t.north = 438 := by
+  obtain ⟨p,hp,rfl⟩ := h
+  rfl
+
+/-- Exact membership in the four finish tiles; their north colors remain
+the two-bit plain/head alternatives rather than an assumed run state. -/
+def FinishTile (t : Tile) : Prop :=
+  ∃ a b : Fin 2, t = ⟨0,432*a.val+b.val,0,438⟩
+
+theorem FinishTile.south {t : Tile} (h : FinishTile t) : t.south = 438 := by
+  obtain ⟨a,b,rfl⟩ := h
+  rfl
+
+/-- Generic connectivity of an open integer interval, with both step
+directions explicit. The predicate need not concern tiles. -/
+theorem interval_propagate (P : ℤ → Prop) (l r x₀ : ℤ)
+    (hl₀ : l < x₀) (hr₀ : x₀ < r) (h₀ : P x₀)
+    (hnext : ∀ x, l < x → x+1 < r → P x → P (x+1))
+    (hprev : ∀ x, l < x-1 → x < r → P x → P (x-1)) :
+    ∀ x, l < x → x < r → P x := by
+  have hright (n : ℕ) : x₀+(n : ℤ) < r → P (x₀+(n : ℤ)) := by
+    induction n with
+    | zero => intro h; simpa only [Nat.cast_zero, add_zero] using h₀
+    | succ n ih =>
+        intro hb
+        have hp := ih (by omega)
+        have hs := hnext (x₀+(n : ℤ)) (by omega) (by omega) hp
+        have he : x₀+((n+1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = (x₀+(n : ℤ))+1 := by omega
+        simpa only [he] using hs
+  have hleft (n : ℕ) : l < x₀-(n : ℤ) → P (x₀-(n : ℤ)) := by
+    induction n with
+    | zero => intro h; simpa only [Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero] using h₀
+    | succ n ih =>
+        intro hb
+        have hp := ih (by omega)
+        have hs := hprev (x₀-(n : ℤ)) (by omega) (by omega) hp
+        have he : x₀-((n+1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = (x₀-(n : ℤ))-1 := by omega
+        simpa only [he] using hs
+  intro x hl hr
+  by_cases hx : x₀ ≤ x
+  · have he : x₀+((x-x₀).toNat : ℤ) = x := by omega
+    have hh := hright (x-x₀).toNat (by omega)
+    simpa only [he] using hh
+  · have he : x₀-((x₀-x).toNat : ℤ) = x := by omega
+    have hh := hleft (x₀-x).toNat (by omega)
+    simpa only [he] using hh
+
+/-- A reset's east1 forces the next tile to reset when that tile is not a seam. -/
+theorem reset_next (T : ℤ → Tile) (x : ℤ)
+    (ha : Allowed (T (x+1))) (hH : (T (x+1)).west = (T x).east)
+    (hn : (T (x+1)).north ≠ 437) (hr : ResetTile (T x)) : ResetTile (T (x+1)) :=
+  west_1_nonseam ha (hH.trans hr.horizontal.2) hn
+
+/-- A reset's west1 forces the previous tile to reset when that tile is not a seam. -/
+theorem reset_previous (T : ℤ → Tile) (x : ℤ)
+    (ha : Allowed (T (x-1))) (hH : (T x).west = (T (x-1)).east)
+    (hn : (T (x-1)).north ≠ 437) (hr : ResetTile (T x)) : ResetTile (T (x-1)) :=
+  east_1_nonseam ha (hH.symm.trans hr.horizontal.1) hn
+
+/-- A single actual reset determines every tile in a connected seam-free
+row segment. Only local interval memberships and matching are needed. -/
+theorem row_reset (T : ℤ → Tile) (l r x₀ : ℤ)
+    (hallowed : ∀ x, l < x → x < r → Allowed (T x))
+    (hH : ∀ x, l < x → x+1 < r → (T (x+1)).west = (T x).east)
+    (hnonseam : ∀ x, l < x → x < r → (T x).north ≠ 437)
+    (hl₀ : l < x₀) (hr₀ : x₀ < r) (hreset : ResetTile (T x₀)) :
+    ∀ x, l < x → x < r → ResetTile (T x) := by
+  apply interval_propagate (fun x => ResetTile (T x)) l r x₀ hl₀ hr₀ hreset
+  · intro x hl hr hx
+    exact reset_next T x (hallowed (x+1) (by omega) hr) (hH x hl hr)
+      (hnonseam (x+1) (by omega) hr) hx
+  · intro x hl hr hx
+    have hh := hH (x-1) hl (by omega)
+    rw [sub_add_cancel] at hh
+    exact reset_previous T x (hallowed (x-1) hl (by omega)) hh
+      (hnonseam (x-1) hl (by omega)) hx
+
+/-- A lone north438 edge suffices because the actual local language first
+identifies its reset tile; an entire reset row is not supplied. -/
+theorem row_reset_of_north438 (T : ℤ → Tile) (l r x₀ : ℤ)
+    (hallowed : ∀ x, l < x → x < r → Allowed (T x))
+    (hH : ∀ x, l < x → x+1 < r → (T (x+1)).west = (T x).east)
+    (hnonseam : ∀ x, l < x → x < r → (T x).north ≠ 437)
+    (hl₀ : l < x₀) (hr₀ : x₀ < r) (hnorth : (T x₀).north = 438) :
+    ∀ x, l < x → x < r → ResetTile (T x) := by
+  exact row_reset T l r x₀ hallowed hH hnonseam hl₀ hr₀
+    ((north_438_iff_reset (hallowed x₀ hl₀ hr₀)).mp hnorth)
+
+/-- Two-dimensional specialization retains the original time and row.
+Vertical matching is unnecessary for this horizontal propagation theorem. -/
+theorem strip_reset_row (T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile) (l r x₀ t : ℤ)
+    (hallowed : ∀ x τ, l < x → x < r → Allowed (T x τ))
+    (hH : ∀ x τ, l < x → x+1 < r → (T (x+1) τ).west = (T x τ).east)
+    (hnonseam : ∀ x τ, l < x → x < r → (T x τ).north ≠ 437)
+    (hl₀ : l < x₀) (hr₀ : x₀ < r) (hreset : ResetTile (T x₀ t)) :
+    ∀ x, l < x → x < r → ResetTile (T x t) := by
+  exact row_reset (fun x => T x t) l r x₀
+    (fun x => hallowed x t) (fun x => hH x t) (fun x => hnonseam x t) hl₀ hr₀ hreset
+
+/-- One south438 edge gives a reset in the next row. Horizontal propagation
+then fixes that entire next interior row, and time matching pulls south438
+back to every tile of the original row. All those original tiles are actual
+finish tiles by the finite language classification. No head, run, or uniform
+finish/reset premise is supplied. -/
+theorem strip_finish_and_reset_of_south438 (T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile) (l r x₀ t : ℤ)
+    (hallowed : ∀ x τ, l < x → x < r → Allowed (T x τ))
+    (hH : ∀ x τ, l < x → x+1 < r → (T (x+1) τ).west = (T x τ).east)
+    (hTime : ∀ x τ, l < x → x < r → (T x (τ+1)).north = (T x τ).south)
+    (hnonseam : ∀ x τ, l < x → x < r → (T x τ).north ≠ 437)

+-- Both induction directions are instantiated at a negative seed; the
+-- interval is not centered at that seed or at the distinguished origin.

+    ∀ x, z-1 < x → x < z+1 → P x := by
+  apply interval_propagate P (z-1) (z+1) z (by omega) (by omega) h
+  · intro x hl hr; omega
+  · intro x hl hr; omega

+/-!
+# The first machine configuration in the derived finite strip
+
+Row encoding means actual north colors in the open interval and an
+interior machine head. It asserts no transition or halting theorem.
+The marked-word initialization theorem derives this encoding for the
+actual machine after its first blank-tape step.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942RowEncoding
+
+open SetTheory.BusyBeaver
+open WangTiles942 WangTiles942Periodic WangTiles942InitialStrip
+  WangTiles942StripGeometry
+
+set_option Elab.async false
+
+/-- Only colors inside the fixed strip are read. No assertion about an
+exterior tape or future machine steps is part of this definition. -/
+structure RowEncodes (T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile) (l r t : ℤ) (cfg : Config 215) : Prop where
+  head_left : l < cfg.head
+  head_right : cfg.head < r
+  north : ∀ x : ℤ, l < x → x < r → (T x t).north = WangMachineEncoding.color cfg x
+
+theorem RowEncodes.color_bound {T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile} {l r t : ℤ} {cfg : Config 215}
+    (h : RowEncodes T l r t cfg) (x : ℤ) (hl : l < x) (hr : x < r) :
+    (T x t).north ≤ 433 := by
+  rw [h.north x hl hr]
+  exact WangMachineEncoding.color_le_433 cfg x
+
+theorem RowEncodes.head_iff {T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile} {l r t : ℤ} {cfg : Config 215}
+    (h : RowEncodes T l r t cfg) (x : ℤ) (hl : l < x) (hr : x < r) :
+    2 ≤ (T x t).north ↔ x = cfg.head := by
+  rw [h.north x hl hr]
+  exact WangMachineEncoding.head_iff cfg x
+
+theorem RowEncodes.plain {T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile} {l r t : ℤ} {cfg : Config 215}
+    (h : RowEncodes T l r t cfg) (x : ℤ) (hl : l < x) (hr : x < r)
+    (hx : x ≠ cfg.head) : (T x t).north = (Tape.read cfg.tape x).toNat := by
+  rw [h.north x hl hr]
+  exact WangMachineEncoding.color_of_ne_head cfg x hx
+
+theorem RowEncodes.operating_head {T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile} {l r t : ℤ} {cfg : Config 215}
+    (h : RowEncodes T l r t cfg) (q : Fin 215) (hq : cfg.state = some q) :
+    (T cfg.head t).north = WangTiles942.headColor q.val (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head).toNat := by
+  rw [h.north cfg.head h.head_left h.head_right, WangMachineEncoding.color_at_head, hq]
+  rfl
+
+/-- Time matching transfers the derived seeded South row to the exact
+initialized machine configuration on the next row. -/
+theorem initialized_row {T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile} {N L R : ℕ}
+    (h : InitialStrip (fun x => T x 0) N L R)
+    (hTime : ∀ x : ℤ, (T x 1).north = (T x 0).south) :
+    RowEncodes T (-(L : ℤ)) (R : ℤ) 1 DecimalMachineInitialization.initialized := by
+  have hl := h.left_pos
+  have hr := h.right_min
+  refine ⟨by change -(L : ℤ) < 1; omega, by change (1 : ℤ) < R; omega, ?_⟩
+  intro x hxl hxr
+  rw [hTime x, initial_south h x hxl hxr, WangMachineEncoding.initialized_color]
+
+/-- The initial configuration is the actual decimal machine at clock1,
+not a separately supplied blank or seeded run. -/
+theorem marked_initialized_strip {N : ℕ} [NeZero N] {s : ℤ} {a : ZMod N → Fin 942}
+    (h : MarkedWord N s a) : ∃ L R : ℕ,
+      PersistentStrip (plane N s a) N L R ∧
+      RowEncodes (plane N s a) (-(L : ℤ)) (R : ℤ) 1
+        (DecimalMachine215.machine.run 1) := by
+  obtain ⟨L,R,hs⟩ := marked_persistent_strip h
+  refine ⟨L,R,hs,?_⟩
+  rw [DecimalMachineInitialization.run_one]
+  exact initialized_row hs.initial (fun x => plane_time_matching h x 0)

+end DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942RowEncoding

+import DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942HeadBounds
+import DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942Signals
+
+/-!
+# Actual machine steps in the derived Wang strip
+
+The operating head writes, its adjacent receiver gets the exact next head
+color, and every other interior tile passes its old bit. Signals cannot
+appear between two plain inputs or enter from a seam wall. Absence of a
+finish row is derived from the operating head, never supplied as a premise.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942RowStep
+
+open SetTheory.BusyBeaver
+open WangTiles942 WangTiles942Language WangTiles942Signals WangTiles942RowEncoding
+  WangTiles942StripGeometry WangTiles942OperatingRow WangTiles942HeadBounds
+
+set_option Elab.async false
+set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000
+set_option maxRecDepth 10000
+
+variable {T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile} {N L R : ℕ} {t : ℤ} {cfg : Config 215}
+
+/-- At the old head the forced transition writes the actual machine bit. -/
+theorem head_south
+    (hA : ∀ x τ, Allowed (T x τ))
+    (hrow : RowEncodes T (-(L : ℤ)) (R : ℤ) t cfg)
+    (q : Fin 215) (hq : cfg.state = some q) :
+    (T cfg.head t).south =
+      (DecimalMachine215.machine.transition q (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)).write.toNat := by
+  rw [head_transition hA hrow q hq, WangMachineAction.transition_write]
+  rfl
+
+/-- A plain cell distinct from the receiving head has no incoming west
+signal. Its left neighbor is a wall, another plain cell, or the inactive
+side of the one actual transition. -/
+theorem far_west_zero
+    (hA : ∀ x τ, Allowed (T x τ))
+    (hH : ∀ x τ, (T (x+1) τ).west = (T x τ).east)
+    (hs : PersistentStrip T N L R)
+    (hrow : RowEncodes T (-(L : ℤ)) (R : ℤ) t cfg)
+    (q : Fin 215) (hq : cfg.state = some q)
+    (x : ℤ) (hl : -(L : ℤ) < x) (hr : x < (R : ℤ))
+    (ho : x ≠ cfg.head)
+    (hn : x ≠ (DecimalMachine215.machine.transition q
+      (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)).move.apply cfg.head) : (T x t).west = 0 := by
+  have hp : (T x t).north = (symbol cfg x).val := hrow.plain x hl hr ho
+  have hm := hH (x-1) t
+  rw [sub_add_cancel] at hm
+  by_cases hw : x-1 = -(L : ℤ)
+  · have hb := left_wall_east_le_two hs t
+    rw [hw] at hm
+    exact plain_west_small_eq_zero (hA x t) (symbol cfg x) hp (by omega)
+  · have hlp : -(L : ℤ) < x-1 := by omega
+    have hrp : x-1 < (R : ℤ) := by omega
+    by_cases hh : x-1 = cfg.head
+    · rw [hh, head_transition hA hrow q hq] at hm
+      cases hd : (action (WangMachineAction.inputIndex q
+          (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head))).2.1 with
+      | false => simpa only [transitionRow, hd, Bool.toNat_false, Nat.zero_mul] using hm
+      | true =>
+          have hmove := WangMachineAction.transition_moved_head q
+            (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head) cfg.head
+          simp only [hd, if_true] at hmove
+          exact False.elim (hn (by omega))
+    · have hz := plain_pair_edge_zero (hA (x-1) t) (hA x t)
+        (symbol cfg (x-1)) (symbol cfg x) (hrow.plain (x-1) hlp hrp hh) hp hm.symm
+      exact hm.trans hz
+
+/-- Symmetric exclusion of an outgoing east signal at an unchanged cell,
+including the actual right wall and the transition's inactive side. -/
+theorem far_east_zero
+    (hA : ∀ x τ, Allowed (T x τ))
+    (hH : ∀ x τ, (T (x+1) τ).west = (T x τ).east)
+    (hs : PersistentStrip T N L R)
+    (hrow : RowEncodes T (-(L : ℤ)) (R : ℤ) t cfg)
+    (q : Fin 215) (hq : cfg.state = some q)
+    (x : ℤ) (hl : -(L : ℤ) < x) (hr : x < (R : ℤ))
+    (ho : x ≠ cfg.head)
+    (hn : x ≠ (DecimalMachine215.machine.transition q
+      (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)).move.apply cfg.head) : (T x t).east = 0 := by
+  have hp : (T x t).north = (symbol cfg x).val := hrow.plain x hl hr ho
+  have hm := hH x t
+  by_cases hw : x+1 = (R : ℤ)
+  · have hb := right_wall_west_le_four hs t
+    rw [hw] at hm
+    exact plain_east_small_eq_zero (hA x t) (symbol cfg x) hp (by omega)
+  · have hlp : -(L : ℤ) < x+1 := by omega
+    have hrp : x+1 < (R : ℤ) := by omega
+    by_cases hh : x+1 = cfg.head
+    · rw [hh, head_transition hA hrow q hq] at hm
+      cases hd : (action (WangMachineAction.inputIndex q
+          (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head))).2.1 with
+      | false =>
+          have hmove := WangMachineAction.transition_moved_head q
+            (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head) cfg.head
+          simp only [hd, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false] at hmove
+          exact False.elim (hn (by omega))
+      | true =>
+          simpa only [transitionRow, hd, Bool.toNat_true, Nat.sub_self, Nat.zero_mul] using hm.symm
+    · exact plain_pair_edge_zero (hA x t) (hA (x+1) t)
+        (symbol cfg x) (symbol cfg (x+1)) hp (hrow.plain (x+1) hlp hrp hh) hm.symm
+
+/-- Both zero edges and the independently derived no-finish theorem force
+the complete pass tuple at every unchanged tape position. -/
+theorem far_pass
+    (hA : ∀ x τ, Allowed (T x τ))
+    (hH : ∀ x τ, (T (x+1) τ).west = (T x τ).east)
+    (hTime : ∀ x τ, (T x (τ+1)).north = (T x τ).south)
+    (hs : PersistentStrip T N L R)
+    (hrow : RowEncodes T (-(L : ℤ)) (R : ℤ) t cfg)
+    (q : Fin 215) (hq : cfg.state = some q)
+    (x : ℤ) (hl : -(L : ℤ) < x) (hr : x < (R : ℤ))
+    (ho : x ≠ cfg.head)
+    (hn : x ≠ (DecimalMachine215.machine.transition q
+      (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)).move.apply cfg.head) :
+    T x t = ⟨0,(Tape.read cfg.tape x).toNat,0,(Tape.read cfg.tape x).toNat⟩ := by
+  exact plain_zero_edges_nonfinish (hA x t) (symbol cfg x) (hrow.plain x hl hr ho)
+    (far_west_zero hA hH hs hrow q hq x hl hr ho hn)
+    (far_east_zero hA hH hs hrow q hq x hl hr ho hn)
+    (no_south438 hA hH hTime hs hrow q hq x hl hr)
+
+/-- The adjacent receiver uses the exact action target and the original
+destination bit. The action may enter halt; target215 is not excluded. -/
+theorem receiver_south
+    (hA : ∀ x τ, Allowed (T x τ))
+    (hH : ∀ x τ, (T (x+1) τ).west = (T x τ).east)
+    (hrow : RowEncodes T (-(L : ℤ)) (R : ℤ) t cfg)
+    (q : Fin 215) (hq : cfg.state = some q)
+    (x : ℤ) (hl : -(L : ℤ) < x) (hr : x < (R : ℤ))
+    (hx : x = (DecimalMachine215.machine.transition q
+      (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)).move.apply cfg.head) :
+    (T x t).south = WangMachineEncoding.headColor
+      (DecimalMachine215.machine.transition q (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)).next
+      (Tape.read cfg.tape x) := by
+  have ho : x ≠ cfg.head := hx ▸ WangMachineStep.moved_head_ne _ _
+  have hp : (T x t).north = (symbol cfg x).val := hrow.plain x hl hr ho
+  have hh := head_transition hA hrow q hq
+  have hmove := WangMachineAction.transition_moved_head q
+    (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head) cfg.head
+  rw [WangMachineAction.transition_headColor]
+  cases hd : (action (WangMachineAction.inputIndex q
+      (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head))).2.1 with
+  | false =>
+      simp only [hd, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false] at hmove
+      have he : x+1 = cfg.head := by omega
+      have hm := hH x t
+      rw [he, hh] at hm
+      have hrx := left_transition_receiver
+        (WangMachineAction.inputIndex q (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)) hd
+        (hA x t) (symbol cfg x) hp hm.symm
+      exact congrArg Tile.south hrx
+  | true =>
+      simp only [hd, if_true] at hmove
+      have he : cfg.head+1 = x := by omega
+      have hm := hH cfg.head t
+      rw [he, hh] at hm
+      have hrx := right_transition_receiver
+        (WangMachineAction.inputIndex q (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)) hd
+        (hA x t) (symbol cfg x) hp hm.symm
+      exact congrArg Tile.south hrx
+
+/-- Every south color is exactly the actual stepped configuration's
+color, by the moved-head / old-head / unchanged three-way partition. -/
+theorem south_step
+    (hA : ∀ x τ, Allowed (T x τ))
+    (hH : ∀ x τ, (T (x+1) τ).west = (T x τ).east)
+    (hTime : ∀ x τ, (T x (τ+1)).north = (T x τ).south)
+    (hs : PersistentStrip T N L R)
+    (hrow : RowEncodes T (-(L : ℤ)) (R : ℤ) t cfg)
+    (q : Fin 215) (hq : cfg.state = some q)
+    (x : ℤ) (hl : -(L : ℤ) < x) (hr : x < (R : ℤ)) :
+    (T x t).south = WangMachineEncoding.color (DecimalMachine215.machine.step cfg) x := by
+  by_cases hn : x = (DecimalMachine215.machine.transition q
+      (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)).move.apply cfg.head
+  · rw [WangMachineStep.color_step _ cfg q hq]
+    simp only [if_pos hn]
+    exact receiver_south hA hH hrow q hq x hl hr hn
+  · by_cases ho : x = cfg.head
+    · subst x
+      rw [WangMachineStep.color_step_old_head _ cfg q hq]
+      exact head_south hA hrow q hq
+    · rw [WangMachineStep.color_step_elsewhere _ cfg q hq x ho hn,
+        WangMachineEncoding.color_of_ne_head cfg x ho]
+      exact congrArg Tile.south (far_pass hA hH hTime hs hrow q hq x hl hr ho hn)
+
+/-- Actual marked-strip row evolution. All native geometry and absence of
+finishes are derived through the frozen component theorems; only actual
+tile matching, persistent walls, an encoded row and a live state enter. -/
+theorem row_step
+    (hA : ∀ x τ, Allowed (T x τ))

+import DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942InputLanguage

+/-!
+# Local signal matching in the actual 942-tile language
+
+Plain-input neighbors cannot match a nonzero signal to one another. A
+transition's outgoing signal forces the appropriate receive tile with exactly
+its actual target, including target 215. No whole-row or run assumption is used.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942Signals
+

+set_option Elab.async false
+set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000
+set_option maxRecDepth 10000

+/-- Only a left-moving receive tile has nonzero east color at a plain input. -/
+theorem plain_east_eq_zero_or_left_receive {t : Tile} (ht : Allowed t)
+    (b : Fin 2) (hn : t.north = b.val) :
+    t.east = 0 ∨ ∃ q : ℕ, q ∈ targets false ∧
+      t = ⟨0,b.val,rail false q,headColor q b.val⟩ := by
+  rcases (north_plain_iff ht b).mp hn with rfl | rfl | ⟨d,q,hq,rfl⟩
+  · exact Or.inl rfl
+  · exact Or.inl rfl
+  · cases d
+    · exact Or.inr ⟨q,hq,by simp⟩
+    · exact Or.inl (by simp)
+
+/-- Only a right-moving receive tile has nonzero west color at a plain input. -/
+theorem plain_west_eq_zero_or_right_receive {t : Tile} (ht : Allowed t)
+    (b : Fin 2) (hn : t.north = b.val) :
+    t.west = 0 ∨ ∃ q : ℕ, q ∈ targets true ∧
+      t = ⟨rail true q,b.val,0,headColor q b.val⟩ := by
+  rcases (north_plain_iff ht b).mp hn with rfl | rfl | ⟨d,q,hq,rfl⟩
+  · exact Or.inl rfl
+  · exact Or.inl rfl
+  · cases d
+    · exact Or.inl (by simp)
+    · exact Or.inr ⟨q,hq,by simp⟩
+
+/-- Small east colors, including every seam west color, force zero. -/
+theorem plain_east_small_eq_zero {t : Tile} (ht : Allowed t)
+    (b : Fin 2) (hn : t.north = b.val) (he : t.east < 6) : t.east = 0 := by
+  rcases plain_east_eq_zero_or_left_receive ht b hn with hz | ⟨q,hq,rfl⟩
+  · exact hz
+  · have hpos := (left_rail_range hq).1
+    simp only at he ⊢
+    omega
+
+/-- Small west colors, including every seam east color, force zero. -/
+theorem plain_west_small_eq_zero {t : Tile} (ht : Allowed t)
+    (b : Fin 2) (hn : t.north = b.val) (hw : t.west < 6) : t.west = 0 := by
+  rcases plain_west_eq_zero_or_right_receive ht b hn with hz | ⟨q,hq,rfl⟩
+  · exact hz
+  · have hpos := (right_rail_range hq).1
+    simp only at hw ⊢
+    omega
+
+/-- Directional rail ranges exclude receive/receive ghost signals. -/
+theorem plain_pair_edge_zero {t u : Tile} (ht : Allowed t) (hu : Allowed u)
+    (b c : Fin 2) (htn : t.north = b.val) (hun : u.north = c.val)
+    (hmatch : t.east = u.west) : t.east = 0 := by
+  rcases plain_east_eq_zero_or_left_receive ht b htn with he | ⟨p,hp,rfl⟩
+  · exact he
+  · rcases plain_west_eq_zero_or_right_receive hu c hun with hw | ⟨q,hq,rfl⟩
+    · have hpos := (left_rail_range hp).1
+      simp only at hmatch ⊢
+      omega
+    · exact False.elim (directional_rails_disjoint hp hq hmatch)
+
+/-- A right transition forces the exact target-bearing receive tile on its right. -/
+theorem right_transition_receiver (j : Fin 430) (hd : (action j).2.1 = true)
+    {u : Tile} (hu : Allowed u) (c : Fin 2) (hn : u.north = c.val)
+    (hmatch : (transitionRow j).2.east = u.west) :
+    u = ⟨rail true (action j).2.2,c.val,0,headColor (action j).2.2 c.val⟩ := by
+  have ht : (action j).2.2 ∈ targets true := by
+    simpa only [hd] using action_target_mem j
+  have he : (transitionRow j).2.east = rail true (action j).2.2 := by
+    simp only [transitionRow, hd, Bool.toNat_true, Nat.one_mul]
+  rw [he] at hmatch
+  rcases plain_west_eq_zero_or_right_receive hu c hn with hw | ⟨q,hq,rfl⟩
+  · have hpos := (right_rail_range ht).1
+    omega
+  · have heq : (action j).2.2 = q := rail_injective_on true ht hq hmatch
+    rw [heq]
+
+/-- A left transition forces the exact target-bearing receive tile on its left. -/
+theorem left_transition_receiver (j : Fin 430) (hd : (action j).2.1 = false)
+    {t : Tile} (ht : Allowed t) (b : Fin 2) (hn : t.north = b.val)
+    (hmatch : t.east = (transitionRow j).2.west) :
+    t = ⟨0,b.val,rail false (action j).2.2,headColor (action j).2.2 b.val⟩ := by
+  have htarget : (action j).2.2 ∈ targets false := by
+    simpa only [hd] using action_target_mem j
+  have hw : (transitionRow j).2.west = rail false (action j).2.2 := by
+    simp only [transitionRow, hd, Bool.toNat_false, Nat.sub_zero, Nat.one_mul]
+  rw [hw] at hmatch
+  rcases plain_east_eq_zero_or_left_receive ht b hn with he | ⟨q,hq,rfl⟩
+  · have hpos := (left_rail_range htarget).1
+    omega
+  · have heq : q = (action j).2.2 := rail_injective_on false hq htarget hmatch
+    rw [heq]
+
+/-- Zero horizontal edges retain both pass and finish until finish is excluded. -/
+theorem plain_zero_edges_iff_pass_or_finish {t : Tile} (ht : Allowed t)
+    (b : Fin 2) (hn : t.north = b.val) :
+    (t.west = 0 ∧ t.east = 0) ↔
+      t = ⟨0,b.val,0,b.val⟩ ∨ t = ⟨0,b.val,0,438⟩ := by
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨hw,he⟩
+    rcases (north_plain_iff ht b).mp hn with hp | hf | ⟨d,q,hq,rfl⟩
+    · exact Or.inl hp
+    · exact Or.inr hf
+    · have hpos := (valid_rail_range hq).1
+      cases d <;> simp only [Bool.toNat_false, Bool.toNat_true, Nat.sub_zero,

+  · rintro (rfl | rfl) <;> exact ⟨rfl,rfl⟩
+

+theorem plain_zero_edges_nonfinish {t : Tile} (ht : Allowed t)
+    (b : Fin 2) (hn : t.north = b.val) (hw : t.west = 0) (he : t.east = 0)
+    (hs : t.south ≠ 438) : t = ⟨0,b.val,0,b.val⟩ := by
+  rcases (plain_zero_edges_iff_pass_or_finish ht b hn).mp ⟨hw,he⟩ with hp | hf
+  · exact hp
+  · exact False.elim (hs (congrArg Tile.south hf))
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942Signals

+import DiophantineConsistency.WangMachineAction
+import DiophantineConsistency.WangMachineStep
+
+/-!
+# Construct the exact Wang row of an actual operating machine step
+
+The old head uses its literal transition tile, the moved head uses the receive
+tile for its actual target and old tape bit, and every other cell passes its bit.
+Entry into halt is included. This constructs a whole-integer matching row; it
+assumes no row/step equivalence or finite-rectangle calibration.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942StepConstruction
+
+open SetTheory.BusyBeaver WangTiles942 WangTiles942Language
+open WangMachineEncoding WangMachineAction WangMachineStep
+
+set_option Elab.async false
+set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000
+set_option maxRecDepth 10000
+
+/-- The action index at the actual old head. -/
+def sourceIndex (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) : Fin 430 :=
+  WangMachineAction.inputIndex q (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)
+
+/-- The moved head from the actual decimal machine transition. -/
+def nextHead (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) : ℤ :=
+  (DecimalMachine215.machine.transition q (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)).move.apply cfg.head
+
+def receiveTile (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) (x : ℤ) : Tile :=
+  let a := WangTiles942.action (sourceIndex cfg q)
+  let b := (Tape.read cfg.tape x).toNat
+  ⟨a.2.1.toNat * rail a.2.1 a.2.2,b,(1-a.2.1.toNat)*rail a.2.1 a.2.2,
+    WangTiles942.headColor a.2.2 b⟩
+
+/-- An explicit whole-integer row; the live-state premise is used only by
+its north/south interpretation, not by the construction itself. -/
+def stepTile (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) (x : ℤ) : Tile :=
+  if x = cfg.head then (transitionRow (sourceIndex cfg q)).2
+  else if x = nextHead cfg q then receiveTile cfg q x
+  else ⟨0,(Tape.read cfg.tape x).toNat,0,(Tape.read cfg.tape x).toNat⟩
+
+theorem nextHead_ne (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) : nextHead cfg q ≠ cfg.head :=
+  moved_head_ne _ _
+
+theorem nextHead_eq (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) :
+    nextHead cfg q = if (WangTiles942.action (sourceIndex cfg q)).2.1
+      then cfg.head+1 else cfg.head-1 :=
+  transition_moved_head q (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head) cfg.head
+
+theorem stepTile_old_head (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) :
+    stepTile cfg q cfg.head = (transitionRow (sourceIndex cfg q)).2 := by
+  simp [stepTile]
+
+theorem stepTile_new_head (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) :
+    stepTile cfg q (nextHead cfg q) = receiveTile cfg q (nextHead cfg q) := by
+  simp [stepTile, nextHead_ne]
+
+theorem stepTile_elsewhere (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) (x : ℤ)
+    (ho : x ≠ cfg.head) (hn : x ≠ nextHead cfg q) :
+    stepTile cfg q x = ⟨0,(Tape.read cfg.tape x).toNat,0,(Tape.read cfg.tape x).toNat⟩ := by
+  simp only [stepTile, if_neg ho, if_neg hn]
+
+theorem receiveTile_allowed (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) (x : ℤ) :
+    Allowed (receiveTile cfg q x) := by
+  exact Allowed.receive _ _ (action_target_mem (sourceIndex cfg q))
+    ⟨(Tape.read cfg.tape x).toNat, by have h := bit_le_one (Tape.read cfg.tape x); omega⟩
+
+/-- Every constructed tile belongs to the actual finite table language. -/
+theorem stepTile_allowed (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) (x : ℤ) :
+    Allowed (stepTile cfg q x) := by
+  by_cases ho : x = cfg.head
+  · subst x
+    rw [stepTile_old_head]
+    exact Allowed.transition _
+  · by_cases hn : x = nextHead cfg q
+    · rw [stepTile, if_neg ho, if_pos hn]
+      exact receiveTile_allowed cfg q x
+    · rw [stepTile_elsewhere cfg q x ho hn]
+      simpa only [Fin.val_zero, Nat.mul_zero, zero_add] using
+        Allowed.pass (0 : Fin 2)
+          ⟨(Tape.read cfg.tape x).toNat, by have h := bit_le_one (Tape.read cfg.tape x); omega⟩
+
+/-- Exact north input, under only the live-state identification. -/
+theorem stepTile_north (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215)
+    (hq : cfg.state = some q) (x : ℤ) : (stepTile cfg q x).north = color cfg x := by
+  by_cases ho : x = cfg.head
+  · subst x
+    rw [stepTile_old_head, color_at_head, hq, operating_head_color]
+    change WangTiles942.headColor ((WangMachineAction.inputIndex q _).val / 2)
+      ((WangMachineAction.inputIndex q _).val % 2) = _
+    rw [inputIndex_div_two, inputIndex_mod_two]
+  · rw [color_of_ne_head cfg x ho]
+    by_cases hn : x = nextHead cfg q
+    · simp only [stepTile, if_neg ho, if_pos hn, receiveTile]
+    · rw [stepTile_elsewhere cfg q x ho hn]
+
+/-- Exact south output of the actual machine step, including entering halt. -/
+theorem stepTile_south (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215)
+    (hq : cfg.state = some q) (x : ℤ) :
+    (stepTile cfg q x).south = color (DecimalMachine215.machine.step cfg) x := by
+  by_cases ho : x = cfg.head
+  · subst x
+    rw [stepTile_old_head, color_step_old_head _ cfg q hq, transition_write]
+    rfl
+  · by_cases hn : x = nextHead cfg q
+    · subst x
+      rw [stepTile_new_head]
+      change WangTiles942.headColor _ _ = color (DecimalMachine215.machine.step cfg)
+        ((DecimalMachine215.machine.transition q (Tape.read cfg.tape cfg.head)).move.apply cfg.head)
+      rw [color_step_new_head _ cfg q hq, transition_headColor]
+      rfl
+    · rw [stepTile_elsewhere cfg q x ho hn,
+        color_step_elsewhere _ cfg q hq x ho hn, color_of_ne_head cfg x ho]
+
+/-- The only west signal is at the old head for left moves, or the new head for right moves. -/
+theorem stepTile_west (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) (x : ℤ) :
+    (stepTile cfg q x).west =
+      if (WangTiles942.action (sourceIndex cfg q)).2.1 then
+        if x = nextHead cfg q then rail true (WangTiles942.action (sourceIndex cfg q)).2.2 else 0
+      else if x = cfg.head then rail false (WangTiles942.action (sourceIndex cfg q)).2.2 else 0 := by
+  have hne := nextHead_ne cfg q

+    cases hd : (WangTiles942.action (sourceIndex cfg q)).2.1 <;>
+    simp_all [stepTile, transitionRow, receiveTile]
+
+/-- The only east signal is at the new head for left moves, or the old head for right moves. -/
+theorem stepTile_east (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) (x : ℤ) :
+    (stepTile cfg q x).east =
+      if (WangTiles942.action (sourceIndex cfg q)).2.1 then
+        if x = cfg.head then rail true (WangTiles942.action (sourceIndex cfg q)).2.2 else 0
+      else if x = nextHead cfg q then rail false (WangTiles942.action (sourceIndex cfg q)).2.2 else 0 := by
+  have hne := nextHead_ne cfg q

+    simp_all [stepTile, transitionRow, receiveTile]

+/-- All horizontal edges match with the actual plane orientation. -/
+theorem stepTile_horizontal (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) (x : ℤ) :

+  rw [stepTile_west, stepTile_east]
+  have hn := nextHead_eq cfg q
+  cases hd : (WangTiles942.action (sourceIndex cfg q)).2.1 <;>
+    simp only [hd, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte] at hn ⊢

+    simp only [he]
+  · have he : x+1 = nextHead cfg q ↔ x = cfg.head := by omega
+    simp only [he]
+
+/-- The constructed row realizes an actual operating step over every integer position. -/
+theorem step_row (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) (hq : cfg.state = some q) :
+    (∀ x : ℤ, Allowed (stepTile cfg q x)) ∧
+    (∀ x : ℤ, (stepTile cfg q x).north = color cfg x) ∧
+    (∀ x : ℤ, (stepTile cfg q x).south = color (DecimalMachine215.machine.step cfg) x) ∧
+    (∀ x : ℤ, (stepTile cfg q (x+1)).west = (stepTile cfg q x).east) :=
+  ⟨stepTile_allowed cfg q, stepTile_north cfg q hq, stepTile_south cfg q hq,
+    stepTile_horizontal cfg q⟩
+

+example (cfg : Config 215) (q : Fin 215) (x : ℤ) :

+import DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942InitialStrip
+import DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942SeamColumns
+
+/-!
+# Fixed finite strip walls and a seam-free interior
+
+The initial row determines the two walls and every interior tile. Actual
+vertical matching preserves the wall columns and excludes seams at every
+interior integer coordinate and time. No machine-run premise is used.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942StripGeometry
+
+open WangTiles942 WangTiles942Language WangTiles942Periodic
+  WangTiles942InitialStrip WangTiles942SeamColumns
+
+set_option Elab.async false
+set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000
+
+/-- The exact initial tile at every integer position strictly between the
+walls. The distinguished South1 and head South4 are retained. -/
+theorem initial_tile {T : ℤ → Tile} {N L R : ℕ} (h : InitialStrip T N L R)
+    (x : ℤ) (hl : -(L : ℤ) < x) (hr : x < (R : ℤ)) :
+    T x = if x < 0 then ⟨2,434,2,0⟩ else
+      if x = 0 then start else if x = 1 then ⟨3,436,4,4⟩ else ⟨4,436,4,0⟩ := by
+  by_cases hx : x < 0
+  · rw [if_pos hx]
+    have hc : ((-x).toNat : ℤ) = -x := Int.toNat_of_nonneg (by omega)
+    have hi := h.left_inside (-x).toNat (by omega) (by omega)
+    simpa only [hc, neg_neg] using hi
+  · rw [if_neg hx]
+    by_cases hz : x = 0
+    · rw [if_pos hz, hz]
+      exact h.start_at_zero
+    · rw [if_neg hz]
+      by_cases ho : x = 1
+      · rw [if_pos ho, ho]
+        exact h.head_at_one
+      · rw [if_neg ho]
+        have hc : (x.toNat : ℤ) = x := Int.toNat_of_nonneg (by omega)
+        have hi := h.right_inside x.toNat (by omega) (by omega)
+        simpa only [hc] using hi
+
+theorem initial_vertical_nonseam {T : ℤ → Tile} {N L R : ℕ}
+    (h : InitialStrip T N L R) (x : ℤ) (hl : -(L : ℤ) < x) (hr : x < (R : ℤ)) :
+    (T x).north ≠ 437 ∧ (T x).south ≠ 437 := by
+  rw [initial_tile h x hl hr]
+  split_ifs <;> decide
+
+/-- This is the seeded tape after the actual blank-machine first action:
+one written1 at zero, state1 on blank0 at position1, and plain0 elsewhere. -/
+theorem initial_south {T : ℤ → Tile} {N L R : ℕ}
+    (h : InitialStrip T N L R) (x : ℤ) (hl : -(L : ℤ) < x) (hr : x < (R : ℤ)) :
+    (T x).south = if x = 0 then 1 else if x = 1 then 4 else 0 := by
+  rw [initial_tile h x hl hr]
+  split_ifs <;> simp_all [start]
+
+/-- Exact initial geometry, persistent seam walls, and no seam inside.
+The finite seam parameters are permitted to change with time. -/
+structure PersistentStrip (T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile) (N L R : ℕ) : Prop where
+  initial : InitialStrip (fun x => T x 0) N L R
+  left_wall : ∀ t : ℤ, ∃ a b : Fin 3, T (-(L : ℤ)) t = ⟨a.val^2,437,b.val,437⟩
+  right_wall : ∀ t : ℤ, ∃ a b : Fin 3, T (R : ℤ) t = ⟨a.val^2,437,b.val,437⟩
+  interior : ∀ x : ℤ, -(L : ℤ) < x → x < (R : ℤ) →
+    ∀ t : ℤ, (T x t).north ≠ 437 ∧ (T x t).south ≠ 437
+
+/-- All temporal geometry follows from allowedness, actual time matching
+and the already derived initial strip; no horizontal premise is added. -/
+theorem persistent_of_initial {T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile} {N L R : ℕ}
+    (hA : ∀ x t, Allowed (T x t))
+    (hTime : ∀ x t, (T x (t+1)).north = (T x t).south)
+    (h : InitialStrip (fun x => T x 0) N L R) : PersistentStrip T N L R := by
+  refine ⟨h, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · exact column_seam_tuples hA hTime (-(L : ℤ)) 0 h.wall_north.1
+  · exact column_seam_tuples hA hTime (R : ℤ) 0 h.wall_north.2
+  · intro x hl hr t
+    have hn := (initial_vertical_nonseam h x hl hr).1
+    have ht : (T x t).north ≠ 437 := by
+      intro hs
+      exact hn ((seam_iff_zero hA hTime x t).mp hs)
+    exact ⟨ht, fun hs => ht ((seam_at_iff_south hA x t).mpr hs)⟩
+
+/-- A marked cyclic word supplies finite fixed strip walls and a seam-free
+interior at every integer time, with only its three actual matching fields. -/
+theorem marked_persistent_strip {N : ℕ} [NeZero N] {s : ℤ} {a : ZMod N → Fin 942}
+    (h : MarkedWord N s a) : ∃ L R : ℕ, PersistentStrip (plane N s a) N L R := by
+  obtain ⟨L,R,hi⟩ := marked_initial_strip h
+  exact ⟨L,R,persistent_of_initial (plane_allowed N s a) (plane_time_matching h) hi⟩
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942StripGeometry

+import DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942StripGeometry
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942StripGeometryChecks
+
+open WangTiles942 WangTiles942Periodic WangTiles942StripGeometry
+
+set_option Elab.async false
+
+/-- The exact initialization is seeded, rather than an everywhere-zero
+South row; the unique operational head has color4. -/
+example {T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile} {N L R : ℕ} (h : PersistentStrip T N L R) :
+    (T 0 0).south = 1 ∧ (T 1 0).south = 4 := by
+  rw [h.initial.start_at_zero, h.initial.head_at_one]
+  exact ⟨rfl,rfl⟩
+
+/-- No assumption about a run, a unique global Start or rectangular
+quotient is needed to obtain the bounded, persistent strip. -/
+example {N : ℕ} [NeZero N] {s : ℤ} {a : ZMod N → Fin 942}
+    (h : MarkedWord N s a) : ∃ L R : ℕ,
+      0 < L ∧ L ≤ N ∧ 2 ≤ R ∧ R ≤ N+1 ∧
+      (∀ x : ℤ, -(L : ℤ) < x → x < (R : ℤ) →
+        ∀ t : ℤ, (plane N s a x t).north ≠ 437 ∧ (plane N s a x t).south ≠ 437) := by
+  obtain ⟨L,R,hs⟩ := marked_persistent_strip h
+  exact ⟨L,R,hs.initial.left_pos,hs.initial.left_le,hs.initial.right_min,
+    hs.initial.right_le,hs.interior⟩
+
+/-- Both distinguished positions lie strictly between the walls, including
+when no additional left or right initializer tail is present. -/
+example {T : ℤ → ℤ → Tile} {N L R : ℕ} (h : PersistentStrip T N L R) (t : ℤ) :
+    (T 0 t).north ≠ 437 ∧ (T 1 t).north ≠ 437 := by
+  have hl := h.initial.left_pos
+  have hr := h.initial.right_min
+  exact ⟨(h.interior 0 (by omega) (by omega) t).1,
+    (h.interior 1 (by omega) (by omega) t).1⟩
+
+#print axioms initial_tile
+#print axioms initial_vertical_nonseam
+#print axioms initial_south
+#print axioms persistent_of_initial
+#print axioms marked_persistent_strip
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.WangTiles942StripGeometryChecks

+SHORTER, CLEARER LEAN PROOFS: DIOPHANTINECONSISTENCY
+Prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov, 26 October 2026
+
+Read report.pdf for the complete source-grounded analysis and priorities.
+report.tex plus validation_summary.tex are the complete editable report source.
+
+REVIEWED SOURCE
+
+Repository: https://github.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt
+Commit: 60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c
+Lean: leanprover/lean4:v4.32.0
+Mathlib: 81a5d257c8e410db227a6665ed08f64fea08e997
+The original repository source was not modified. No patch was applied or
+published remotely. This archive is a proposal/prototype deliverable.
+
+WHAT IS INCLUDED
+
+report.pdf / report.tex
+    Detailed review: priorities; exact source locations; proof-only changes;
+    witness layouts; checked-history folds; scanners; residual aggregation;
+    existing DAG certificates; native arithmetic; object-model semantics;
+    import-layer changes; adoption and validation criteria.
+
+lean/
+    Modules selected for successful Lean 4.32.0 replay. The authoritative
+    per-file status and scope are in evidence/validation_manifest.json.
+    LookupAPI.lean and ValidatedFold.lean use Std only.
+    NativeRefactorCore.lean uses the core omega tactic.
+    WitnessLayout.lean imports the actual Representation module and includes
+    rfl checks of equality with the original constructor expressions.
+    SplitPowerCertificate.lean uses the actual SplitCircuit59 module.
+    GapExactDataFixture.lean contains a byte-for-byte extracted naturalNodes
+    definition and checks only the needed topology, power, and dispatch facts.
+    It is not a full rebuild of the original GapCircuit66 module.
+
+proposals/
+    Additional production integration candidates. These files are explicitly
+    not all replayed as full project modules. Do not treat their presence as
+    a claim of compilation. Consult the validation manifest before adoption.
+    Compile them individually; the Gap fixture and its production candidate
+    intentionally expose some corresponding declaration names.
+
+patches/lookup-api.patch
+    Exact proof-only patch: seven list-lookup induction proofs become calls
+    to existing Lean library lemmas, saving 40 physical lines across five
+    source files. The generic replacement terms compile; git apply --check
+    passes. The five entire patched modules have not been replayed here.
+
+evidence/
+    Source hashes and inventory; import graph; declaration index; exact
+    component metrics; Lean compiler/axiom logs; fixture byte-identity data;
+    independent source-review notes; validation limits.
+
+scripts/
+    inventory.py: comment-aware, reproducible lexical source measurements.
+    replay.py: focused replay of the checked modules, without applying patch.
+    check_gap_fixture.py: verify exact fixture/source definition bytes.
+    generate_power_certificate.py: regenerate exponent-label certificates.
+    generate_gap_fixture.py: regenerate the exact-data Gap validation fixture.
+
+REPLAY
+
+Use a complete ProveIt checkout at the commit above and its pinned Lean.
+Install/copy dependencies and the matching Mathlib compiled cache using the
+repository's usual setup. The following focused cache command was used:
+
+    lake exe cache get Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.Eval Mathlib.Tactic
+
+From this archive directory:
+
+    python3 scripts/replay.py /absolute/path/to/ProveIt --core-only
+    python3 scripts/replay.py /absolute/path/to/ProveIt
+
+The script refuses a different commit, checks the Lean version, runs patch
+applicability, builds only needed parent imports for the selected examples,
+and saves new logs under replay-results/. It does not modify packaged evidence
+or apply the patch. Use the Python 3 executable name appropriate to your OS.
+
+Reproduce the inventory:
+
+    python3 scripts/inventory.py /absolute/path/to/ProveIt --output new-inventory
+
+Regenerate certificates into a separate temporary directory:
+
+    python3 scripts/generate_power_certificate.py \
+      /absolute/path/to/ProveIt/Computability/DiophantineConsistency/Lean/DiophantineConsistency \
+      /absolute/path/to/temporary-certificates
+
+The fixture generator also needs CircuitDispatch.lean in that temporary
+prototype directory (copy it from proposals/ first). The generated fixture
+contains the copied naturalNodes definition and a uniform power certificate.
+Python label checks are diagnostic. Lean checking is the proof.
+
+After ordinary repository checks pass, the small patch may be reviewed/applied
+with git apply. Rebuild its affected project modules and their public audit
+endpoints before merging it. This review did not perform that final integration.
+
+REBUILD THE REPORT
+
+XeLaTeX, fontspec, unicode-math, fvextra, and the Latin Modern / DejaVu Sans
+Mono fonts are required. Run twice in this directory:
+
+    xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error report.tex
+    xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error report.tex
+
+INTERPRETING THE MEASUREMENTS
+
+546 active Lean files contain 73,971 physical lines. The two generated Steps
+files contain 6,567 lines, 999 step declarations, and 193 power declarations.

+
+No compilation-speedup benchmark is claimed. An unmodified GapCircuit66
+compilation was terminated with exit code 137. Its exact-data fixture is a
+separate, narrower validation route with an explicit byte-identity manifest.
+
+MATHEMATICAL SCOPE
+
+The proposals preserve the intended semantic boundaries: host arithmetic,
+arbitrary-model internal naturals, and syntactic ZFC derivability are distinct.
+The offset-19 theorem excludes 510 while permitting the actual 511 self-loop;
+offset-20 works for an arbitrary function. Cyclic geometry includes N=1 and
+arbitrary wrapped shifts. These proof refactorings do not establish any new
+end-to-end consistency equivalence or complete pending machine/label binding.
+
+All successful theorem audits in the final ledger use only the standard
+propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound axioms (some use fewer or none).
+The delivered checked examples do not rely on sorryAx or native-evaluation
+axioms. See the manifest for which full imports and which isolated fixtures
+were actually replayed.

+Independent mathematical/source review of compiler prototypes
+
+Reviewed files:
+  review-work/compiler/WitnessLayout.lean
+  review-work/compiler/GapPowerCertificate.lean
+  review-work/compiler/SplitPowerCertificate.lean
+  review-work/compiler/CircuitDispatch.lean
+
+Compared against pinned source commit
+60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c, specifically Representation.lean,
+ArithmeticDAGSemantics.lean, ArithmeticDAGPowers.lean, GapCircuit66.lean,
+and SplitCircuit59.lean. This is an independent source/mathematical review;
+the compiler agent owns compilation and axiom audit results.
+
+Verdict: I found no mathematical circularity, changed circuit data, or lost
+assumption in the four reviewed prototypes. The claims are appropriately
+local. They do not establish any new end-to-end consistency equivalence.
+
+1. WitnessLayout
+
+The renaming lemma is just a pointwise equality of the same natAssignment
+functions. The witness-splitting equivalence is constructive: restrictions
+use Fin.castAdd and Fin.natAdd, and combination uses Fin.addCases. It does
+not invoke choice or assume represented predicates are decidable.
+
+conjunctionCompact builds precisely the old witnessCount r+s and the same
+sum of two squares after the same renamings. disjunctionCompact builds the
+same product after the same renamings. The proofs use only r.correct and
+s.correct, not correctness of the old conjunction/disjunction constructors.
+The examples comparing expression fields by rfl substantiate literal
+expression preservation; witness-count preservation is also apparent from
+the constructor definitions. Zero-filled unused witness blocks are valid
+because Rep quantifies natural witnesses, including zero. The helper also
+handles an empty witness block.
+
+Permissible claim: these two representation constructors have factored
+proofs with definitionally unchanged expression data and unchanged witness
+counts. Do not claim they reduce polynomial degree or variable counts.
+
+2. GapPowerCertificate and SplitPowerCertificate
+
+Both certificates refer directly to the original naturalNodes, with no new
+node list, index map, output expression, or rewiring. The imported literal
+circuit modules do not import their corresponding generated Steps files.
+label_steps is a finite kernel-checked proposition about the actual nodes.
+It is therefore independent of the old pure-power proof chains.
+
+The existing run_power theorem performs strong induction on node index.
+Actual Topological evidence makes both multiplication operands earlier
+than the current node. A positive label at a non-base node requires two
+nonzero operand labels and an additive exponent equation. No power value
+identity is assumed as an input. At the base, exponent one gives a
+tautological identity. Hence the certificate is not circular.
+
+Label zero means 'not certified as a power', not exponent zero. The public
+power theorem correctly retains hp : label i != 0. No identity is claimed
+for any zero-labelled node. The exact bounds i<484 and i<515 are converted
+using each original natural_length theorem. This blocks default getD
+behavior from introducing an out-of-range node into the conclusion.
+
+The Gap example proves value(node375)=value(node20)^2200. The Split
+example proves value(node407)=value(node36)^1201. These identities are
+valid over every commutative ring with the same symbolic fixed parameters
+and inputs as the original circuits. They do not specialize or calibrate
+the fixed parameters and do not identify the entire output with a target
+Diophantine equation.
+
+Permissible claim: a checked finite exponent certificate derives the
+same local pure-power facts for the literal naturalNodes, replacing the
+need for their repeated algebraic chains. Do not claim every generated
+step or semantic recipe theorem can be deleted: non-power nodes, named
+semantic cut points, and final recipe correctness still need proofs.
+
+3. CircuitDispatch
+
+reg is an abbreviation through the existing value evaluator, not a freely
+chosen value assignment. step specializes the already-proved
+run_node_equation to the original Gap naturalNodes and its topology proof.
+It therefore assumes neither the desired node equation nor the candidate
+base identity. The i<484 bound rules out out-of-range nodes.
+
+base_identity selectively expands nodes 20,18,19,10,0,9 and uses ring. This
+is a local algebraic identity for the literal circuit. The step theorem is
+not globally registered as a simp lemma, which avoids silently expanding
+the entire DAG recursively.
+
+Permissible claim: named local step lemmas can be obtained on demand from
+the generic evaluator theorem, and the illustrated base identity follows
+without a pre-generated theorem for every intermediate node. This alone
+does not replace all semantic cut points or prove the full circuit recipe.
+
+4. Remaining presentation/validation boundaries
+
+- Cite the compiler agent's replay/axiom logs separately; this review did
+  not rebuild the files.
+- Count the new certificate lists and helpers when reporting net source
+  reduction. Short local proof bodies are not automatically a net project
+  reduction.
+- Distinguish proof-only changes from expression/DAG transformations. All
+  four prototypes reviewed here preserve the original relevant data.
+- A coefficient/source snapshot hash records provenance but is not itself
+  a proof. Soundness here comes from literal-node checks, topology, and
+  Lean's theorem checking.
+- No consistency, ZFC interpretation, positivity calibration, machine
+  simulation, or end-to-end Diophantine equivalence is newly proved here.

+Independent source review of NativeRefactorCore.lean
+Reviewer: annotated/object-layer review agent
+Compared against ProveIt 60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c
+No new build performed; this is a source/interface review.
+
+Conclusion: no hidden hypothesis strengthening or invalid generalization found
+in the half-radix lemmas or CarryCertificate.recurrence. The generic lemmas are
+appropriate helper interfaces. They remain proposals until the existing client
+theorems are instantiated and replayed.
+
+1. halfRadix_exact (prototype lines 13-16)
+   The identity follows by factoring the same positive s out of both the
+   remainder and quotient. The condition 0 < s is necessary for the quotient
+   cancellation: at s = 0 the proposed right side would still contain b / 2.
+   The prototype states that condition explicitly. No digit bound is needed.
+
+2. halfRadix_bound (19-24)
+   This is a valid strengthening of NativeCyclicRotation.shiftDigits_half_bound
+   (original lines 100-116): instantiate a = c k and b = c (k - 1). The original
+   hypothesis hc supplies b <= 3. The current digit a need not be bounded,
+   because a % 2 <= 1 for every natural a. The bound s + 1 is unchanged.
+   No cyclic-size, NeZero, or phase-alignment hypothesis is added.
+
+3. halfRadix_parity (27-32)
+   Valid: even s removes the first term modulo 2; b <= 3 ensures b / 2 < 2,
+   which is exactly why the final remainder can be removed. For the original
+   shiftDigits_half_parity_89 (160-165), take s = 2^88, a = c k, b = c (k - 1).
+   Positivity and evenness follow numerically, and 2 * 2^88 = 2^89 is the only
+   radix normalization needed. The new evenness premise is not an extra
+   assumption in the original fixed-radix theorem; it is already true of its
+   concrete scale. A wrapper should discharge it rather than expose it to
+   existing callers. The current 2011 window uses radix 2^47, so analogous use
+   there requires s = 2^46; do not silently substitute the old 89-bit constants.
+
+4. quotient_of_decomposition / remainder_of_decomposition (51-61)
+   digit < radix supplies radix > 0, so there is no missing zero-radix case.
+   The equation total = digit + radix * carry fixes both quotient and remainder
+   by the usual natural division identities. These lemmas do not prove that a
+   decomposition exists, nor that different cyclic carry assignments coincide.
+
+5. CarryCertificate.recurrence (65-75)
+   Its assumptions are a subset/repackaging of the original Facts fields:
+     radix := CurrentKernel2011.radix
+     budget := 57
+     raw i := convolution folded c i + binaryRotation 47 W c i
+     prev i := i - 1
+     carry := k
+   Facts.digit_bound (line 59) and Facts.carry_equation (63-66) imply the exact
+   existing Facts.carry_recurrence (60-62). Facts.carry_bound supplies carry_le
+   if the nested certificate is used, but is not needed for recurrence itself.
+   Therefore dropping the stored recurrence and restoring it as a theorem
+   projection is mathematically sound. The abstraction over arbitrary I adds no
+   injectivity, finiteness, nonemptiness, or cyclic-permutation assumption.
+
+Integration cautions:
+- Preserve the theorem name/accessor Facts.carry_recurrence so downstream code
+  can keep using f.carry_recurrence i after the field becomes a derived theorem.
+- The existing endpoint polynomial_zero_window has positional record assembly
+  at lines 140-141. Removing or nesting fields requires updating that assembly;
+  named fields would make future changes safer.
+- Do not make CarryCertificate an added hypothesis of polynomial_zero_window.
+  It must still be constructed from the actual positive polynomial zero using
+  the existing source_carries extraction. Otherwise the endpoint would be
+  weakened by moving its conclusion into a premise.
+- Keep digit bounds and the global word/mask/source facts. The quotient lemma
+  only makes the recurrence field redundant; it does not replace normalization
+  existence, mask semantics, or the entire Facts record.
+- Claims should concern redundancy of the proof field and source reuse, not
+  a reduction in polynomial coordinates or computational witness size.
+
+Secondary check: forall_lt_by_chunks is valid without r < B. Its tail hypothesis
+explicitly covers all j < r, so allowing a longer tail does not leave a gap.

+import Lean.Elab.Tactic.Omega
+
+/-!
+Kernel-checkable arithmetic helpers for a proposed DiophantineConsistency
+refactoring.  These are new helper lemmas, not replacements already integrated
+into ProveIt.  Checked with Lean 4.32.0 and no Mathlib dependency.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.RefactorPrototype
+
+/-- The exact half-radix shift; unlike finite-case proofs this applies to
+arbitrary input digits and any positive scale. -/
+theorem halfRadix_exact {s : Nat} (hs : 0 < s) (a b : Nat) :
+    (s * a) % (2 * s) + (s * b) / (2 * s) =
+      s * (a % 2) + b / 2 := by
+  rw [Nat.mul_comm 2 s, Nat.mul_mod_mul_left, Nat.mul_div_mul_left _ _ hs]
+
+/-- The existing digits-at-most-three bound follows from the exact formula. -/
+theorem halfRadix_bound {s a b : Nat} (hs : 0 < s) (hb : b ≤ 3) :
+    (s * a) % (2 * s) + (s * b) / (2 * s) ≤ s + 1 := by
+  rw [halfRadix_exact hs]
+  have hm : a % 2 ≤ 1 := by omega
+  have hm' := Nat.mul_le_mul_left s hm
+  omega
+
+/-- Parity at an even half-radix needs only the predecessor bound. -/
+theorem halfRadix_parity {s a b : Nat} (hs : 0 < s) (heven : s % 2 = 0)
+    (hb : b ≤ 3) :
+    ((s * a) % (2 * s) + (s * b) / (2 * s)) % 2 = b / 2 := by
+  rw [halfRadix_exact hs, Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, heven]
+  simp only [Nat.zero_mul, Nat.zero_mod, Nat.zero_add, Nat.mod_mod]
+  exact Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (by omega)
+
+/-- Dispatch an index to one of q full blocks and a final short block.
+Individual block facts may remain separate kernel-checked declarations. -/
+theorem forall_lt_by_chunks {P : Nat → Prop} {B q r : Nat} (hB : 0 < B)
+    (hblocks : ∀ k, k < q → ∀ j, j < B → P (B * k + j))
+    (htail : ∀ j, j < r → P (B * q + j)) :
+    ∀ i, i < B * q + r → P i := by
+  intro i hi
+  by_cases hfull : i < B * q
+  · have hk : i / B < q :=
+      (Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hB).mpr (by simpa only [Nat.mul_comm] using hfull)
+    have h := hblocks (i / B) hk (i % B) (Nat.mod_lt i hB)
+    simpa only [Nat.div_add_mod] using h
+  · have h := htail (i - B * q) (by omega)
+    simpa only [Nat.add_sub_of_le (by omega : B * q ≤ i)] using h
+
+/-- With a bounded remainder, exact local decomposition already determines
+the quotient.  A normalization record need not store both facts. -/
+theorem quotient_of_decomposition {radix total digit carry : Nat}
+    (hdigit : digit < radix) (hlocal : total = digit + radix * carry) :
+    carry = total / radix := by
+  rw [hlocal, Nat.add_mul_div_left _ _ (by omega), Nat.div_eq_of_lt hdigit,
+    Nat.zero_add]
+
+/-- The remainder is likewise determined by the same decomposition. -/
+theorem remainder_of_decomposition {radix total digit carry : Nat}
+    (hdigit : digit < radix) (hlocal : total = digit + radix * carry) :
+    digit = total % radix := by
+  rw [hlocal, Nat.add_mul_mod_self_left, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hdigit]
+
+/-- A proof certificate for an existing carry assignment.  Construction of
+this certificate must still be proved from the actual equation. -/
+structure CarryCertificate {I : Type} (radix budget : Nat)
+    (raw : I → Nat) (prev : I → I) (carry digits : I → Nat) : Prop where
+  carry_le : ∀ i, carry i ≤ budget
+  digit_lt : ∀ i, digits i < radix
+  decompose : ∀ i, raw i + carry (prev i) = digits i + radix * carry i
+
+theorem CarryCertificate.recurrence {I : Type} {radix budget : Nat}
+    {raw : I → Nat} {prev : I → I} {carry digits : I → Nat}
+    (h : CarryCertificate radix budget raw prev carry digits) (i : I) :
+    carry i = (raw i + carry (prev i)) / radix :=
+  quotient_of_decomposition (h.digit_lt i) (h.decompose i)
+
+#print axioms halfRadix_exact
+#print axioms halfRadix_bound
+#print axioms halfRadix_parity
+#print axioms forall_lt_by_chunks
+#print axioms quotient_of_decomposition
+#print axioms remainder_of_decomposition
+#print axioms CarryCertificate.recurrence
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.RefactorPrototype

+import Std

+/-!
+# A shared proof kernel for checked history folds
+
+Prototype for ProveIt commit 60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c.
+This module does not replace any repository declaration. It isolates the
+recursion common to AnnotatedRename, AnnotatedBound, and AnnotatedProofChecker.
+It uses Lean's standard library only and makes no model-theoretic assertion.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.Proposals.ValidatedFold
+
+variable {Line Judgment : Type}
+
+def run (valid : Line → List Judgment → Bool) (emit : Line → Judgment) :
+    List Line → List Judgment → Option (List Judgment)
+  | [], seen => some seen
+  | line :: lines, seen =>
+      if valid line seen then run valid emit lines (emit line :: seen) else none
+
+theorem run_append (valid : Line → List Judgment → Bool) (emit : Line → Judgment)
+    (p q : List Line) (seen : List Judgment) :
+    run valid emit (p ++ q) seen =
+      (run valid emit p seen).bind (run valid emit q) := by
+  induction p generalizing seen with
+  | nil => rfl
+  | cons line lines ih =>
+    simp only [List.cons_append, run]
+    split <;> simp_all
+
+theorem run_sound (valid : Line → List Judgment → Bool) (emit : Line → Judgment)
+    (P : Judgment → Prop)
+    (local_sound : ∀ line seen, (∀ j ∈ seen, P j) →
+      valid line seen = true → P (emit line))
+    (lines : List Line) (seen result : List Judgment)
+    (hseen : ∀ j ∈ seen, P j) (h : run valid emit lines seen = some result) :
+    ∀ j ∈ result, P j := by
+  induction lines generalizing seen with
+  | nil => cases h; exact hseen
+  | cons line lines ih =>
+    simp only [run] at h
+    split at h
+    next hv =>
+      apply ih _ _ h
+      intro j hj
+      cases List.mem_cons.mp hj with
+      | inl hj => exact hj ▸ local_sound line seen hseen hv
+      | inr hj => exact hseen j hj
+    next hv => contradiction
+
+def Produces (valid : Line → List Judgment → Bool) (emit : Line → Judgment)
+    (lines : List Line) (history : List Judgment) : Prop :=
+  ∀ seen, run valid emit lines seen = some (history ++ seen)
+
+theorem Produces.append
+    {valid : Line → List Judgment → Bool} {emit : Line → Judgment}
+    {p q : List Line} {hp hq : List Judgment}
+    (h₁ : Produces valid emit p hp) (h₂ : Produces valid emit q hq) :
+    Produces valid emit (p ++ q) (hq ++ hp) := by
+  intro seen
+  rw [run_append, h₁ seen]
+  simp only [Option.bind_some]
+  rw [h₂ (hp ++ seen), List.append_assoc]
+
+theorem Produces.step
+    {valid : Line → List Judgment → Bool} {emit : Line → Judgment}
+    {p : List Line} {history : List Judgment}
+    (hp : Produces valid emit p history) (line : Line)
+    (hv : ∀ seen, valid line (history ++ seen) = true) :
+    Produces valid emit (p ++ [line]) (emit line :: history) := by
+  intro seen
+  rw [run_append, hp seen]
+  simp only [Option.bind_some, run, hv seen, if_true, List.cons_append]
+
+/- The following generic recurrence is definitionally the scan recurrence
+used by the repository. It does not require Nat-pairing or a chosen encoding. -/
+def scan {State : Type} (step : State → State) (fuel : Nat) (initial : State) : State :=
+  fuel.rec initial (fun _ acc => step acc)
+
+theorem scan_succ {State : Type} (step : State → State) (fuel : Nat) (initial : State) :
+    scan step (fuel + 1) initial = scan step fuel (step initial) := by
+  induction fuel with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | succ fuel ih =>
+    change step (scan step (fuel + 1) initial) = step (scan step fuel (step initial))
+    rw [ih]
+
+theorem scan_fixed {State : Type} (step : State → State) (fixed : State)
+    (hfixed : step fixed = fixed) (fuel : Nat) : scan step fuel fixed = fixed := by
+  induction fuel with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | succ fuel ih =>
+    change step (scan step fuel fixed) = fixed
+    rw [ih, hfixed]
+
+#print axioms run_append
+#print axioms run_sound
+#print axioms Produces.append
+#print axioms Produces.step
+#print axioms scan_succ
+#print axioms scan_fixed
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.Proposals.ValidatedFold

+import DiophantineConsistency.Representation
+
+/-!
+Prototype for a small, data-preserving witness-layout API.
+The original repository files are not modified.  These definitions use the
+same witness counts and expressions as Rep.conjunction and Rep.disjunction.
+-/
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.ProofSimplification
+
+variable {σ τ ι κ : Type*}
+
+@[simp] theorem natAssignment_comp_sumMap
+    (v : τ → ℕ) (w : κ → ℕ) (f : σ → τ) (g : ι → κ) :
+    natAssignment v w ∘ Sum.map f g = natAssignment (v ∘ f) (w ∘ g) := by
+  funext i
+  cases i <;> rfl
+
+theorem eval_rename_natAssignment (e : Expr (σ ⊕ ι))
+    (v : τ → ℕ) (w : κ → ℕ) (f : σ → τ) (g : ι → κ) :
+    (e.rename (Sum.map f g)).eval (natAssignment v w) =
+      e.eval (natAssignment (v ∘ f) (w ∘ g)) := by
+  rw [Expr.eval_rename, natAssignment_comp_sumMap]
+
+/-- Move between a single concatenated witness block and its two components. -/
+theorem exists_split_witnesses {m n : ℕ}
+    (P : (Fin m → ℕ) → (Fin n → ℕ) → Prop) :
+    (∃ w : Fin (m + n) → ℕ,
+      P (w ∘ Fin.castAdd n) (w ∘ Fin.natAdd m)) ↔
+        ∃ a b, P a b := by
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨w, hw⟩
+    exact ⟨w ∘ Fin.castAdd n, w ∘ Fin.natAdd m, hw⟩
+  · rintro ⟨a, b, h⟩
+    refine ⟨Fin.addCases a b, ?_⟩
+    simpa [Function.comp_def] using h
+
+variable {P Q : (σ → ℕ) → Prop}
+
+/-- Same data as Rep.conjunction, with common layout reasoning factored out. -/
+def conjunctionCompact (r : Rep σ P) (s : Rep σ Q) : Rep σ (fun v => P v ∧ Q v) := by
+  let left := r.expression.rename (Sum.map id (Fin.castAdd s.witnessCount))
+  let right := s.expression.rename (Sum.map id (Fin.natAdd r.witnessCount))
+  refine ⟨r.witnessCount + s.witnessCount, left * left + right * right, ?_⟩
+  intro v
+  simp only [left, right, Expr.eval_add, Expr.eval_mul,
+    eval_rename_natAssignment, Function.comp_id, mul_self_add_mul_self_eq_zero]
+  rw [exists_split_witnesses (m := r.witnessCount) (n := s.witnessCount)
+    (fun a b => r.expression.eval (natAssignment v a) = 0 ∧
+      s.expression.eval (natAssignment v b) = 0), r.correct, s.correct]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨⟨a, ha⟩, ⟨b, hb⟩⟩
+    exact ⟨a, b, ha, hb⟩
+  · rintro ⟨a, b, ha, hb⟩
+    exact ⟨⟨a, ha⟩, ⟨b, hb⟩⟩
+
+/-- Same data as Rep.disjunction; the unused witness block is filled by zero. -/
+def disjunctionCompact (r : Rep σ P) (s : Rep σ Q) : Rep σ (fun v => P v ∨ Q v) := by
+  let left := r.expression.rename (Sum.map id (Fin.castAdd s.witnessCount))
+  let right := s.expression.rename (Sum.map id (Fin.natAdd r.witnessCount))
+  refine ⟨r.witnessCount + s.witnessCount, left * right, ?_⟩
+  intro v
+  simp only [left, right, Expr.eval_mul, eval_rename_natAssignment,
+    Function.comp_id, mul_eq_zero]
+  rw [exists_split_witnesses (m := r.witnessCount) (n := s.witnessCount)
+    (fun a b => r.expression.eval (natAssignment v a) = 0 ∨
+      s.expression.eval (natAssignment v b) = 0), r.correct, s.correct]
+  constructor

+import DiophantineConsistency.ArithmeticDAGSemantics
+import DiophantineConsistency.GapCircuit66
+
+/-! On-demand specialization of the existing local-node theorem.
+This prototype deliberately leaves named semantic cut points in place.
+It is not a global simp rule: unbounded recursive rewriting would inline the DAG.
+-/
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.ProofSimplification.CircuitDispatch
+open ArithmeticDAG
+set_option maxRecDepth 30000
+set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000
+
+variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
+
+def reg (p : Fin 11 → R) (x : Fin 9 → R) (i : ℕ) : R :=
+  value GapCircuit66.naturalNodes i p x
+
+theorem step (p : Fin 11 → R) (x : Fin 9 → R) (i : ℕ) (hi : i < 484) :
+    reg p x i = (GapCircuit66.naturalNodes.getD i (.literal 0)).evalAt p x (reg p x) :=
+  run_node_equation p x GapCircuit66.naturalNodes GapCircuit66.natural_topological i
+    (by simpa only [GapCircuit66.natural_length] using hi)
+
+-- The statement has exactly the same content as natural_step_20.
+example (p : Fin 11 → R) (x : Fin 9 → R) :
+    reg p x 20 = reg p x 18 * reg p x 19 :=
+  step p x 20 (by decide)
+
+-- Selective specialization keeps the base as the intended cut point.
+theorem base_identity (p : Fin 11 → R) (x : Fin 9 → R) :
+    reg p x 20 = p 0 * (x 0 + 1)^2 := by
+  simp only [step p x 20 (by decide), step p x 18 (by decide),
+    step p x 19 (by decide), step p x 10 (by decide),
+    step p x 0 (by decide), step p x 9 (by decide),
+    GapCircuit66.naturalNodes, List.getD_cons_zero, List.getD_cons_succ, Node.evalAt, Fin.mk_zero]
+  ring
+
+#print axioms base_identity
+end DiophantineConsistency.ProofSimplification.CircuitDispatch

+import DiophantineConsistency.QuarticCost

+
+/-! Reusable executable sum-of-squares lemmas.  These move duplicated semantic
+and cost arguments into a public API without changing any polynomial data. -/
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.ProofSimplification.CompilerCommon
+
+variable {σ : Type*}
+
+@[simp] theorem eval_sumExpressions (es : List (Expr σ)) (v : σ → ℤ) :
+    (QuarticSyntax.sumExpressions es).eval v = (es.map (fun e => e.eval v)).sum := by
+  induction es <;> simp_all [QuarticSyntax.sumExpressions]
+
+def sumSquares {n : ℕ} (rows : Fin n → Expr σ) : Expr σ :=
+  QuarticSyntax.sumExpressions (List.ofFn fun i => rows i * rows i)
+
+theorem sumSquares_zero_iff {n : ℕ} (rows : Fin n → Expr σ) (v : σ → ℤ) :
+    (sumSquares rows).eval v = 0 ↔ ∀ i, (rows i).eval v = 0 := by
+  rw [sumSquares, eval_sumExpressions]
+  simp only [List.map_ofFn, Fin.sum_ofFn, Function.comp_apply, Expr.eval_mul]
+  simpa only [Finset.mem_univ, forall_true_left] using
+    (Finset.sum_mul_self_eq_zero_iff (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))
+      (fun i => (rows i).eval v))
+
+theorem sumSquares_degree {n d : ℕ} (rows : Fin n → Expr σ)
+    (hd : ∀ i, (rows i).toPolynomial.totalDegree ≤ d) :
+    (sumSquares rows).toPolynomial.totalDegree ≤ 2*d := by
+  rw [sumSquares, QuarticSyntax.polynomial_sumExpressions]
+  simp only [List.map_ofFn, Fin.sum_ofFn, Function.comp_apply, Expr.toPolynomial]
+  apply MvPolynomial.totalDegree_finsetSum_le
+  intro i _
+  simpa only [two_mul] using
+    (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_mul (rows i).toPolynomial (rows i).toPolynomial).trans
+      (Nat.add_le_add (hd i) (hd i))
+
+theorem sumExpressions_cost (es : List (Expr σ)) (b : ℕ)
+    (h : ∀ e ∈ es, e.binaryOps ≤ b) :
+    (QuarticSyntax.sumExpressions es).binaryOps ≤ (b+1)*es.length := by
+  induction es with
+  | nil => simp [QuarticSyntax.sumExpressions, Expr.binaryOps]
+  | cons e es ih =>
+    have he := h e (by simp)
+    have ht := ih (fun e he => h e (by simp [he]))
+    change 1 + e.binaryOps + (QuarticSyntax.sumExpressions es).binaryOps ≤ _
+    simp only [List.length_cons, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one]
+    omega
+
+/-- Existing weighted-degree machinery supplies unweighted degree for free. -/
+theorem unweighted_degree (e : Expr σ) :
+    e.toPolynomial.totalDegree ≤ e.weightedDegree (fun _ => 1) := by
+  simpa only [Expr.evalRing_X] using
+    e.degree_evalRing_le (fun _ => 1) MvPolynomial.X (fun _ => by simp)
+
+#print axioms sumSquares_zero_iff
+#print axioms sumSquares_degree
+end DiophantineConsistency.ProofSimplification.CompilerCommon

+
+/-! Prototype showing that the natural gate proofs are instances of the
+already proved semiring results.  Integrating it requires splitting gate data
+out of QuarticCompiler to avoid an import cycle; this file is an independent
+validation of the semantic bridge, not that module reorganization. -/
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.ProofSimplification.SemiringSpecialization
+open QuarticCompiler.Gates
+
+variable {σ τ : Type*}
+
+theorem zero_iff_semiringZero (e : Expr (σ ⊕ τ)) (v : σ → ℕ) (w : τ → ℕ) :
+    e.eval (natAssignment v w) = 0 ↔ e.SemiringZero (semiringAssignment v w) := by
+  have ha : natAssignment v w = fun i => (semiringAssignment v w i : ℤ) := by
+    funext i
+    cases i <;> rfl
+  rw [ha, Expr.eval_eq_zero_iff_splitNatural]
+  simp only [Expr.SemiringZero, NatExpr.evalSemiring_nat]
+
+theorem values_nat (e : NatExpr σ) (v : σ → ℕ) :
+    semiringValues e v = values e v := by
+  induction e with
+  | constant n => rfl
+  | var i => rfl
+  | add p q hp hq | mul p q hp hq =>
+    funext k
+    rcases k with k | (k | k)
+    · simp only [semiringValues, values, NatExpr.evalSemiring_nat]
+    · exact congrFun hp k
+    · exact congrFun hq k
+
+theorem complete_from_semiring (e : NatExpr σ) (v : σ → ℕ) (k : Wire e) :
+    (residualSyntax e k).eval (natAssignment v (values e v)) = 0 := by
+  apply (zero_iff_semiringZero _ _ _).mpr
+  simpa only [values_nat] using semiring_complete e v k
+
+theorem sound_from_semiring (e : NatExpr σ) (v : σ → ℕ) (w : Wire e → ℕ)
+    (h : ∀ k, (residualSyntax e k).eval (natAssignment v w) = 0) :
+    w (root e) = e.eval v := by
+  simpa only [NatExpr.evalSemiring_nat] using
+    semiring_sound e v w (fun k => (zero_iff_semiringZero _ _ _).mp (h k))
+
+#print axioms complete_from_semiring
+#print axioms sound_from_semiring
+end DiophantineConsistency.ProofSimplification.SemiringSpecialization

+\section{Findings and priorities}
+
+The best route to shorter proofs is to make the repeated mathematical
+interfaces explicit, then retain the original executable objects and prove
+their correctness through those interfaces. In this project, proof length,
+the size of a represented program, the size of a polynomial, and the cost of
+kernel checking are separate quantities. A successful proof refactor can
+leave all program and polynomial data definitionally unchanged.
+
+There are three especially promising levels of work.
+First, small proof-only changes can immediately remove local induction and
+transport boilerplate. Second, a few reusable semantic APIs can replace
+the same list, witness, and sum-of-squares arguments in several modules.
+Third, the generated circuit proof files can use the certificate machinery
+already proved in the repository, substantially reducing their materialized
+proof source while retaining named semantic intermediate results.
+

+\toprule
+Order & Proposal & Evidence or deliverable & Effort\\\midrule
+\endfirsthead
+\toprule Order & Proposal & Evidence or deliverable & Effort\\\midrule
+\endhead
+1 & Replace seven list-lookup inductions & Exact patch; 40 physical lines saved & Small\\
+2 & Share witness-layout semantics & Compact constructors with expression-equality checks & Small\\
+3 & Share checked-history folds and scan recurrences & Six generic laws, checked in Lean & Small--medium\\
+4 & Centralize executable sum-of-squares semantics & Three repeated evaluation proofs; shared degree/cost API & Small--medium\\

+6 & Specialize local DAG equations on demand & 999 existing per-index wrappers & Medium\\

+\bottomrule

+
+The order reflects risk and ease of review, rather than a claim that the
+earliest item yields the largest line reduction. The power certificate work
+offers the largest concrete component compression; the witness and scanner
+interfaces offer the strongest improvement to day-to-day proof maintenance.
+Several further ideas are developed below: a dynamic-seed primitive-recursive
+iterator, Boolean reflection, a small copied-field interface, and disciplined
+proof profiling.
