+# Circuit, representation, and quartic proof review
+
+Snapshot: `60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c`.
+All source paths below are relative to
+`Computability/DiophantineConsistency/Lean/DiophantineConsistency/`.
+Status of executable examples belongs to their check logs; this review does
+not infer Lean acceptance from a successful Python computation.
+
+Validation obtained in this review: the import-free
+`AssignmentTransportCore.lean` compiles with Lean 4.32.0, exit 0; its theorem
+`sumElim_comp_sumMap` uses only `[Quot.sound]`. The separate
+project-dependent `AssignmentTransport.lean` did not complete validation:
+direct checking aborted at the explicitly imposed 1 GiB Lean memory cap,
+without a theorem diagnostic. The circuit patch, DAG prototypes, and
+sum-of-squares prototypes have not been kernel-replayed in this review.
+Their source-data checks and the exact shared-tail comparison succeeded.
+
+## 1. Fix the generator to respect previously established semantic cuts
+
+The most concrete immediate improvement is in
+`SplitCircuitRegisters59.lean:103-110,130-137`. The theorem
+`natural_sourceSRegister` expands register 393 to individual kernel registers,
+although `natural_sourceHighRegister` was already proved at lines 94-101.
+The theorem `natural_sourceRankRegister` similarly expands the circuits for
+block length, source S, and source T despite their immediately preceding
+semantic interface theorems. This is unnecessary re-proving of already named
+expressions. The corresponding Gap66 proofs already use the better discipline.
+
+The supplied `split-register-cuts.patch` changes the generator and regenerated
+proof file together. When building the list of entries, it snapshots the
+current map of known semantic cuts and then adds the theorem just scheduled:
+
+```python
+entries.append((name, idx, expr, dict(cuts), False, defs))
+cuts[idx] = name
+```
+
+The copy is essential. Saving a reference to the same mutable `cuts` dictionary
+would let an earlier entry see its own theorem or a later theorem. Proofs must
+only depend on cuts emitted earlier. The patch also removes the obsolete
+unfolding of `sourceHigh`, `sourceS`, `sourceT`, and `blockLength` from consumers
+that now use their established register equations.
+
+Measured source changes:
+
+| Existing theorem | Rewrite rules before | After | UTF-8 bytes before | After |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| `natural_sourceSRegister` | 19 | 7 | 744 | 487 |
+| `natural_sourceRankRegister` | 36 | 9 | 1,142 | 555 |
+
+The generated Lean source decreases by 844 bytes, from 14,604 to 13,760.
+Each theorem still occupies eight physical lines, because the existing file
+prints each rewrite list on one very long line. Claiming a line-count reduction
+here would be misleading. The meaningful reduction is the number of facts and
+definitions exposed to the algebraic normalizer. No circuit data, theorem
+statement, assumptions, or witness counts change. Generator source grows by
+one physical line; generated source byte savings exceed that small addition.
+
+The patch should be replayed by compiling the regenerated module, checking
+its downstream clients, and running the generator's `--check` mode in an
+isolated patched tree. A regeneration check alone is not a proof check.
+
+## 2. Extract the genuinely shared 99-node free-carrier tail
+
+This is a stronger architectural opportunity than shortening rewrite lists.
+The `ratioValue` definitions in `SplitNinePolynomial59.lean:58-81` and
+`GapNinePolynomial66.lean:59-82` are exactly equal as source text: 24 lines and
+612 UTF-8 bytes. They describe the same free-carrier finalizer with twelve
+ring-valued inputs. Their source/rank front ends differ.
+
+More strongly, source-data inspection establishes that the complete suffix
+of the Split natural circuit at indices 416 through 514 and the complete
+suffix of the Gap natural circuit at indices 385 through 483 are the same
+99 nodes after changing references. Internal references decrease by 31.
+The external boundary references are mapped as follows:
+
+| Split register | Gap register | Interpretation |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 7 | 7 | Internal j input |
+| 9 | 9 | One |
+| 10 through 17 | Same index | Shifted input values |
+| 21 | 87 | Two |
+| 409 | 378 | Threshold N |
+| 414 | 383 | Rank |
+| 415 | 384 | Margin scale |
+
+The supplied `inspect_shared_tail.py` repeats this equality test from the
+pinned inert generator node dictionaries. It first checks the repository
+commit, loads the two existing read-only generators (which check the JSON
+SHA256 pins), confirms byte-for-byte regeneration of both circuit files and
+both step files, extracts the suffixes, renames references, and checks exact
+dictionary equality. All four regeneration comparisons pass. The JSON receipt
+is `shared-tail-evidence.json`. This establishes a concrete refactoring
+target; it is not yet a Lean theorem that the refactoring preserves evaluation.
+
+Proposed interface:
+
+1. Define a small arithmetic block syntax whose operand is either a named
+   boundary port or an earlier local node. The 99-node block has 14 boundary
+   ports, including one and two, and no dependence on the source encodings.
+2. Define its interpretation over an arbitrary commutative ring, and prove
+   once that insertion into a parent DAG preserves its interpretation when
+   the boundary-register values agree.
+3. Prove once that this block evaluates to the shared `ratioValue` function.
+   This replaces the duplicated sequence of 24 named tail-register identities
+   in `SplitCircuitRecipe59.naturalValue_eq_recipe` and
+   `GapCircuitRecipe66.naturalValue_eq_recipe`.
+4. Certify by closed kernel checking that each existing parent suffix is an
+   instantiation of this block. Reuse the current front-end source-register
+   facts to discharge the 14 boundary bindings.
+
+The insertion operation should instantiate references directly, adding no
+copy gates. Otherwise the refactor would change the carefully counted circuit
+data. Include an equality theorem between the generated parent node list and
+the pinned original list, not only an equality of sampled outputs. The block
+proof should live below both Split and Gap specializations, importing only
+the generic DAG machinery and common free-carrier algebra. Do not make either
+specialization import the other solely to reuse its tail theorem.
+
+There is a typing detail worth treating explicitly: Split has 12 fixed
+coefficient inputs whereas Gap has 11. The existing `NodeRel` assumes the same
+input and fixed-input counts on both sides. The shared tail has no fixed-input
+leaf reads, so a boundary-port block avoids pretending the two parent `Node`
+types are identical. It also makes the dependency on front-end values precise.
+
+This proposal does not claim to remove 99 nodes or to reduce the Diophantine
+equation size. It removes duplicated reasoning about a 99-node subprogram.
+The source and checking-time savings need to be measured after implementation.
+
+## 3. Reuse the existing circuit abstraction; do not rebuild it in a tactic
+
+`ArithmeticDAGSemantics.lean` already provides the crucial facts:
+
+- `run_node_equation` at lines 58-94 gives a local equation for every valid
+  node of a topological circuit.
+- `run_eq_of_node_equations` at lines 97-109 proves uniqueness of a proposed
+  evaluation table satisfying the local equations.
+- `value_eq_of_node_equations` at lines 111-117 gives the output version.
+
+`ArithmeticDAGPowers.lean` already contains an actual small certificate
+checker: `PowerStep`, `run_power`, `NodeRel`, `PowerRewriteStep`, and
+`value_eq_of_powerRewrite`. `SplitJointPower59` instantiates this checker.
+The project is therefore already pursuing the right separation between
+finite data and generic proof. An effective next refactor expands this
+existing architecture to reusable blocks and semantic cuts.
+
+The two generated step files contain 6,567 physical lines and 323,610 bytes:
+
+| File | Lines | Ordinary step theorems | Power theorems |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| `SplitCircuitSteps59.lean` | 3,445 | 515 | 107 |
+| `GapCircuitSteps66.lean` | 3,122 | 484 | 86 |
+
+These are mechanically generated specializations of existing generic facts,
+not 1,192 independent mathematical arguments. Avoid reporting deletion of
+generated lines as an equivalent reduction of hand-maintained proof logic.
+A generic indexed API or lazy proof-producing command could avoid emitting
+unused specializations, but should be benchmarked against the current named
+lemmas: the named lemmas provide efficient rewrite boundaries and stable
+dependency granularity. A global simp rule that unfolds every register can
+destroy sharing and expose a very large expression tree.
+
+## 4. One assignment-transport law replaces repeated Sum/Fin bookkeeping
+
+`Representation.lean` repeatedly proves that renaming an expression's input
+and witness coordinates is equivalent to precomposing its assignments. The
+same `rw [Expr.eval_rename]; congrArg; funext; cases` proof occurs in
+`Rep.reindex`, both witness sides of `Rep.conjunction`, and both witness sides
+of `Rep.disjunction` (roughly lines 157-220).
+
+The supplied `AssignmentTransport.lean` isolates the general identity
+
+```lean
+natAssignment v w ∘ Sum.map f g =
+  natAssignment (v ∘ f) (w ∘ g)
+```
+
+and its semantic consequence
+
+```lean
+(e.rename (Sum.map f g)).eval (natAssignment v w) =
+  e.eval (natAssignment (v ∘ f) (w ∘ g))
+```
+
+The first proof is just function extensionality and a case split on the sum;
+the second uses `Expr.eval_rename`. This is a good stable simp direction:
+move renamings out of the expression evaluator and into the assignment.
+Do not also install the converse as a simp rule. `Fin.castAdd` and `Fin.natAdd`
+become instances of the generic law, with no repeated coordinate proof.
+
+The immediate number of deleted lines is modest, especially after charging
+the helper statements themselves. The useful change is that witness layout
+is certified in one place. The representation data and witness counts remain
+definitionally the same. This is preferable to replacing executable `Rep`
+constructors by existentially chosen representations.
+
+## 5. Centralize sum-of-squares facts and parameterize the existing cost bound
+
+The same private three-line `eval_sumExpressions` lemma occurs verbatim in
+`DAGQuartic.lean:83-85`, `NaturalDAGQuartic.lean:110-112`, and
+`QuadraticRegisterSystem.lean:70-72`. Each then repeats the same passage from
+a finite sum of squared residuals to pointwise vanishing.
+
+Publish `QuarticSyntax.eval_sumExpressions` and a single theorem for an
+arbitrary finite residual family. The supplied `CircuitCoreRefactors.lean`
+contains this exact general statement and proof. Each existing
+`expression_zero_iff` becomes a direct application after unfolding only its
+expression constructor. The reduction is an ordinary mathematical interface,
+not a new tactic or trusted evaluator.
+
+Keep the codomain assumption honest. Sum of squares implies pointwise zero
+over the integers in these files; it is false for a general commutative ring.
+The separate internal-omega reasoning in `ObjectResidualSquares` cannot be
+replaced by an integer theorem without proving the required transfer. It
+operates on positive/negative semiring interpretations in the actual object
+theory, a stronger and different requirement.
+
+`QuarticCost.sumExpressions_binaryOps_le` is currently specialized to residual
+squares costing at most five operations, while `DAGQuartic.sumExpressions_cost`
+reproves the parameterized result privately. Publish the parameterized bound
+once and keep the old specialized theorem as a compatibility corollary.
+The existing sharp output contributions should remain separate: uniformly
+bounding every residual would weaken `12 * nodes.length + 4` to a larger
+constant and would discard information unnecessarily.
+
+The private `degree_add` and `degree_sub` helpers are also duplicated between
+the signed and nonnegative DAG quartic compilers. A shared degree API should
+serve both. Their different wire encodings and witness counts remain distinct.
+
+## 6. Factor the topology induction only when it earns its place
+
+`ArithmeticDAGSemantics.run_eq_of_node_equations`,
+`NaturalDAGQuartic.run_nonnegative`, and
+`ArithmeticDAGDegree.value_degree_le` each repeat strong induction, a call
+to `run_node_equation`, and conversion of dependency membership to a smaller
+node index. A general `run_invariant` lemma captures exactly this argument:
+if each gate preserves a property from its predecessor values, then every
+evaluated register has the property.
+
+`CircuitCoreRefactors.lean` includes the helper and three same-statement
+replacement proofs. It retains the topology hypothesis. It can be used for
+additional range bounds, algebraic invariants, and semantic-table uniqueness.
+
+This is not currently a net source-shortening result. Under the supplied
+formatting, the three original declarations occupy 42 lines/2,083 UTF-8 bytes;
+the helper plus three proposed versions occupy 45 lines/2,296 bytes, including
+the longer `_short` names. The benefit is one induction proof instead of
+three. A fourth useful client would better amortize the interface. Treat it
+as a maintainability option, below the direct reuse and shared-tail changes.
+
+## 7. Share the positive/natural circuit-translation proof
+
+`SplitCircuitTranslation59.lean` and `GapCircuitTranslation66.lean` are both
+79 lines. Their proofs have the same structure: handle eleven initial
+registers, exclude the stored unshifted register 7, handle one swapped
+multiplication, and use a closed finite reference certificate for the rest.
+The special multiplication index is 452 in Split and 421 in Gap.
+
+A generic input-translation/reference-simulation theorem can expose these
+parameters and consume the existing finite certificate. An extension of
+`NodeRel` that allows operand swapping for addition and multiplication would
+eliminate the one ad hoc `ring` case in each instantiation. Subtraction must
+retain ordered operands.
+
+The existing `ArithmeticDAG.run_map` and `value_map` are already the correct
+tools for changing the *ring of values*, and are used to obtain polynomial
+identities. They cannot by themselves prove positive/natural translation:
+the two node lists differ, and `x ↦ x - 1` is not a ring homomorphism. Use
+the semantic reference certificate to relate the lists, and naturality only
+for transporting the resulting identity between coefficient rings.
+
+## 8. Preserve the distinction between natural inputs and nonnegative wires
+
+The names `SplitCircuit59.naturalNodes` and `GapCircuit66.naturalNodes` refer
+to external input conventions. Those circuits contain negative literal
+coefficients and subtraction. They do not meet
+`NaturalDAGQuartic.NodeAllowed`, which excludes subtraction and requires
+nonnegative constants. Reusing the one-natural-variable-per-gate compiler
+requires its actual `Allowed` proof. Names are not such a proof.
+
+Similarly, `NaturalRegisterProgram.Op` deliberately has only natural literals,
+inputs, addition, and multiplication. It is an excellent foundation for
+nonnegative register programs, but simply forcing signed finalizers through
+it would change semantics or assumptions. A common block interface should be
+ring-valued for the Split/Gap tail and keep the positive compiler as a
+specialization with explicit nonnegativity evidence.
+
+## Suggested priority
+
+1. Apply the semantic-cut generator patch and replay it.
+2. Add assignment-transport and sum-of-squares helper APIs with compatibility
+   wrappers; simplify their existing clients.
+3. Extract the common `ratioValue` algebra and certify the 99-node shared tail.
+4. Generalize positive/natural reference simulation, including commutative
+   operand swaps in the finite relation.
+5. Consider generic `run_invariant` only with clear additional clients.
+6. Benchmark indexed/lazy step theorem generation before replacing the current
+   generated named facts.
+
+For every phase, compare exact theorem statements, axiom footprints, actual
+compiled circuit data, clean checking time, and proof-source size including
+new helpers. Separate source-data checks, kernel proof checks, and performance
+measurements in the report.

+# Annotated checkers and object-level proofs: refactoring audit
+
+Baseline: ProveIt commit `60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c`, Lean `v4.32.0`, mathlib commit `81a5d257c8e410db227a6665ed08f64fea08e997`. All source anchors below are under `Computability/DiophantineConsistency/Lean/DiophantineConsistency/` unless stated otherwise.
+
+## 1. Immediate small patch: use existing list facts
+
+The archive candidate `lookup-cleanup.patch` replaces seven inductive proofs in five files without changing any theorem statement, definition, supplied program, node count, or public name. The net change is **40 physical source lines removed**.
+
+| Target | Baseline lines | Replacement |
+|---|---:|---|
+| `AnnotatedRename.lookup_mem` | 110–117 | `exact List.mem_of_getElem? h` |
+| `AnnotatedBound.lookup_mem` | 50–57 | same |
+| `AnnotatedProofChecker.mem_of_lookup` | 177–187 | same |
+| `AnnotatedRuleSide.lookup_mem` | 18–25 | same |
+| `AnnotatedAssumption.lookup_mem` | 40–47 | same |
+| `AnnotatedRuleSide.exists_lookup` | 27–35 | `exact List.getElem?_of_mem h` |
+| `AnnotatedAssumption.exists_lookup` | 49–57 | same |
+
+Both library lemmas are in the exact toolchain's `Init/Data/List/Lemmas.lean`, at lines 469 and 479. `LookupCleanup.lean` kernel-checks both polymorphic replacement statements with no project assumptions. Both depend only on `propext` according to `#print axioms`. The `List.getElem?_of_mem` form is preferable here to `(List.mem_iff_getElem?).mp`: the latter happens to include `Quot.sound` in its dependency closure in this toolchain, while the direct lemma does not.
+
+`git apply --check` succeeds against the pinned repository. The full five patched modules have **not** been rebuilt. The scope of evidence is exact polymorphic statement checking plus patch applicability, not an integration build. This is a modest, genuinely measured reduction; do not extrapolate it to an overall percentage.
+
+## 2. Consolidate the scanner proof pattern
+
+Five modules define the same `fuel.rec initial (fun _ state => step state)` iterator and separately prove `scan_zero`, `scan_succ`, and `scan_done`:
+
+| Family | Iterator lemma block |
+|---|---:|
+| `AnnotatedRenameScan` | 34–55 |
+| `AnnotatedBoundScan` | 30–51 |
+| `AnnotatedLineScan` | 35–54 |
+| `AnnotatedContext` | 100–119 |
+| `AnnotatedAxiomContext` | 32–50 |
+
+These 15 proof bodies contain **72 physical lines**, excluding signatures. They express generic iteration facts. Mathlib already provides `Function.iterate_succ_apply`, `Function.iterate_fixed`, and `Function.iterate_succ_apply'` in `Mathlib/Logic/Function/Iterate.lean` (lines 65, 91, 174). Production should reuse them after proving one bridge for the current `Nat.rec` convention, or use a small prelude-only helper matching that convention exactly. The supplied `ScannerCore.lean` implements the latter so its proof does not depend on obtaining the whole project build.
+
+The more useful abstraction goes beyond those small lemmas. The following simulation appears repeatedly:
+
+* `AnnotatedRenameScan.scan_table`, lines 71–87;
+* `AnnotatedBoundScan.scan_table`, lines 67–83;
+* `AnnotatedLineScan.scan_list`, lines 135–159;
+* `AnnotatedAxiomContext.scan_list`, lines 130–151.
+
+All four consume one encoded list cell per step, move to an updated history when validation succeeds, absorb rejection at zero, and stop changing after the list is exhausted. `ScannerCore.Encoding` isolates precisely three obligations for each concrete encoding:
+
+1. the rejecting state is fixed;
+2. the encoded empty-list state is fixed;
+3. the step on an encoded cons agrees with a supplied typed transition `next : Row -> History -> Option History`.
+
+The proved theorem is:
+
+```lean
+scan_run (e : Encoding next step) (rows : List A) (history : H)
+    (fuel : Nat) (enough : rows.length ≤ fuel) :
+  iterate step fuel (e.state rows history) = e.result (run next rows history)
+```
+
+This lets the row-specific `step_cons` and validator correctness theorem retain the mathematical content, while one induction handles list consumption, sufficient fuel, rejection, and the terminal state. Existing numeric definitions need not change; a bridge to the generic `run` or a variant of `Encoding` carrying the existing runner equations suffices. The file has not yet been integrated, so no net source reduction or runtime improvement is claimed for this framework. Count helper code and adapters as well as removed inductions when evaluating the migration.
+
+The generic core is **kernel-checked with Lean 4.32.0**. Its seven theorems all have an empty axiom dependency list. There is no `sorry`, added axiom, `native_decide`, or custom evaluator.
+
+### Preserve raw-input soundness
+
+`scan_run` is about encoded typed inputs. It does not itself establish correctness for arbitrary natural codes. The current project carefully proves that stronger fact separately, especially in `AnnotatedLineScan.scan_sound` (58–86), `AnnotatedAxiomContext.scan_sound` (53–85), and `AnnotatedContext.scan_sound` (122–145). Keep that distinction.
+
+For LineScan and AxiomContext, use the generic forward iteration invariant
+
+```text
+P(state) := state = reject OR
+  there exist a remaining raw code and a genuine, semantically good history
+  whose encoding is state.
+```
+
+The checker-specific local soundness theorem supplies the one-step preservation proof. `ScannerCore.iterate_invariant` supplies the induction. For Context, where the step consumes two sides of a relation, use the checked `iterate_preimage` theorem: if `P(step s)` implies `P(s)`, terminal validity pulls back along any fuel bound. Do not replace these all-code statements with claims only about successfully parsed syntax.
+
+## 3. Share typed execution and proof-fragment composition
+
+The duplication starts before numeric encoding. Compare:
+
+* `AnnotatedRename.lean`, `run`, `run_append`, `run_sound`, `Produces`, `Produces.append`, `Produces.step`, lines 192–235;
+* `AnnotatedBound.lean`, the same pattern, lines 132–175;
+* `AnnotatedProofChecker.lean`, corresponding definitions and lemmas, lines 201–250.
+
+They differ mainly in the row validator, the semantic predicate on accepted outputs, and the function selecting the new history entry. A generic `run next` plus a one-step invariant proves all the repeated `run_sound` inductions; `ScannerCore.run_invariant` and `run_append` are checked versions of these two general facts.
+
+The fragment predicate `Produces p h := forall seen, run p seen = some (h ++ seen)` has an identical append law in all three families. Factor it in a separate, small list-history layer rather than putting syntax-specific assumptions in the scanner core. Preserve the **reversed order of histories**: executing `p ++ q` prepends `hq ++ hp`, not `hp ++ hq`. Backward parent references depend on this order. This is an easy place for an aesthetically cleaner API to change behavior accidentally.
+
+The per-rule completeness constructions (`ready_binary`, `ready_unary`, `fragment2`, `fragment3`) can then use a single certified fragment-composition interface. Start by eliminating the duplicated infrastructure; do not encode the seventeen original rules into a new calculus solely to save lines.
+
+## 4. Keep program data while sharing the primitive-recursion combinator
+
+`AnnotatedBoundScan.P`, `AnnotatedLineScan.P`, and `AnnotatedAxiomContext.P` repeat `scannerBase`, `scannerBaseProgram`, `scannerRecursion`, `scannerRecursionProgram`, and `scannerProgram`. The key blocks are BoundScan 144–158, LineScan 231–245, AxiomContext 218–232. Their base history differs (zero for judgment tables, one for the encoded empty axiom context), and the chosen fuel projection also differs.
+
+A generic `iterateProgram` should accept supplied base/step/fuel programs and build their `.prec` composition once. Its correctness proof can reuse `Realizes.prec` and the iterator bridge. This is a program-construction refactor, not merely a proof refactor: retain or reprove exact `.val` equality and node-count equalities before claiming the same concrete supplied checker. A bare proof that a function is primitive recursive would discard the data needed for later polynomial and size constructions.
+
+The existing `ScalarPRCode.Realizes`, `.comp`, `.pair`, `.prec`, and `.ofEq` are already the right basis (`ScalarPRCode.lean`, lines 48–91). Do not propose rebuilding that existing abstraction.
+
+## 5. Extract object-model proof wrappers; generalize the arity of local transport
+
+The exact string `completeness_inf_context ZFCax_s []` occurs **26 times in 17 `Object*.lean` files**. The repeated shell obtains a model, extracts `ZFAxioms`, invokes `seal_valid`, and finally performs a local semantic argument. Good targets include:
+
+* `ObjectNaturalExpression.zfc_proves_total` and `.zfc_proves_unique`, lines 182–202;
+* `ObjectCodeClosure` lines 153–167;
+* `ObjectCodeBound` lines 458–472;
+* `ObjectCodeSeal` lines 93–106;
+* `ObjectPairingGraph` lines 92–117;
+* `ObjectResidualSquares.zfc_proves_residual_conjunction`, lines 170–182.
+
+A proved wrapper for obtaining `BProv ZFCax_s [] (sealF phi)` from validity of `phi` in every relevant model would remove the same four setup lines repeatedly. Keep the model-universe quantification and the existing completeness theorem explicit. It is a logical transport lemma, not permission to infer internal ZFC statements from an arbitrary external theorem about standard naturals.
+
+A particularly small local improvement is in `ObjectQuarticCompiler.zfc_proves_compiler`, lines 106–116. The local helper
+
+```lean
+have closed (f : Expr (Fin m)) : ...
+```
+
+forces a duplicate `closedTarget` proof because the compiled expression has a different arity. Generalize it to
+
+```lean
+have closed {n : ℕ} (f : Expr (Fin n)) : ...
+```
+
+and use it for both `e` and `compiledExpression e`. This preserves the theorem and removes an entire repeated environment-invariance argument. The generalized helper body uses the same `ObjectPolynomial.sat_noZeroForm_iff` and `Sat_sentence_inv` lemmas. This local edit has been source-inspected but not compiled in the project.
+
+## 6. Build on the algebraic interface that already exists
+
+The repository already proves that the entire internal omega forms a commutative semiring (`ObjectOmegaSemiring`), adds an order/cancellation layer (`ObjectNaturalOrder`), and provides semiring gate/compiler semantics (`GatesSemiring`, `QuarticSemiring`). A proposal to add those interfaces from scratch would miss the current state of the project.
+
+The next consolidation opportunity is to move model-independent downstream statements into the existing algebraic layer. For example, `ObjectQuadraticSystem.conjunction_rows_zero_iff` (22–32) repeats the finite-index argument in `QuadraticRegisterComposition.System.conjunction_holds` (33–46), and the instantiation proofs have the same renaming/composition structure. A generic predicate over a family of rows, together with a general evaluation/renaming lemma, can serve both standard-natural assignments and arbitrary internal-natural assignments.
+
+`ObjectResidualSquares` similarly contains an algebraic argument about a cancellative, canonically ordered semiring with no zero divisors, after the necessary model-specific facts are already installed. Its proof is not allowed to identify internal omega with external `Nat`. Also, do not import `ObjectNaturalOrderedSemiring` directly into it: the current dependency goes through `ObjectNaturalDiscrete` back to `ObjectResidualSquares`, so that would introduce a cycle. Extract a lower-level algebraic lemma with only the needed assumptions, or reorganize the dependency graph deliberately.
+
+Finally, be careful with `ObjectNaturalExpression.evalRel_unique`: its current statement has **no assumption that every input lies in omega**. Replacing it by a semiring-evaluation argument that requires all inputs to be natural would weaken the API. The totality theorem can profit from a semiring witness under its existing natural-input hypotheses; uniqueness needs either the existing proof or a generic functional-relational evaluator lemma that retains its stronger statement.
+
+## Implementation order
+
+1. Apply the seven list-library replacements and run the affected checks.
+2. Share iteration lemmas across all five scanners without modifying numeric programs.
+3. Integrate `Encoding`/`scan_run` into RenameScan and BoundScan, then LineScan and AxiomContext; compare total source and elaboration cost.
+4. Factor typed-run/fragment infrastructure and the PR iterator constructor, preserving supplied program data and exact size facts.
+5. Extract object-model validity transport and arity-polymorphic sentence helpers.
+6. Consolidate downstream algebraic proofs only after drawing the import graph and checking that theorem hypotheses are unchanged.
+
+The supplied `verification.log` and `verified-files.sha256` describe exactly the checked artifacts. They do not certify a full-project migration or prove the project's still-separate consistency calibration.

+\section*{Executive assessment}
+\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Executive assessment}
+
+The best opportunities are concentrated in repeated mathematical interfaces:
+encoded-list scanners, coordinate renamings, finite coefficient rows, and the
+composition of already certified circuit blocks. A uniform substitution of
+\code{simp}, \code{aesop}, or a larger heartbeat limit would miss these targets.
+
+There are useful changes at three scales. First, seven private list-lookup
+proofs can use two existing Lean-core lemmas; the supplied patch removes
+40 physical lines. Second, a common arithmetic identity removes the
+half-radix case analysis, and one row-wise argument can replace hundreds of
+lines of repeated coefficient bounds. Third, the Split and Gap natural
+circuits have an exactly matching 99-node suffix under a specified register
+renaming. A reusable block for that suffix is the most concrete larger
+architectural target identified here.
+
+Some abstractions are worthwhile without shortening the file immediately.
+For example, a common topological-DAG invariant theorem can replace repeated
+strong inductions. After charging for the new helper, the first few clients
+do not yet yield a net line saving. The report states this explicitly instead
+of treating every abstraction as a compression result.
+
+Several elementary examples were checked with the pinned Lean compiler.
+Larger replacements and full scanner/circuit migrations have separate status
+labels in Section~\ref{sec:validation} and the archive's verification record.
+The strongest source comparisons are accompanied by scripts and exact data.

+\label{sec:scope}
+
+The inspected snapshot is the main-branch commit recorded above. The active
+source root is \code{Computability/DiophantineConsistency/Lean}. Its physical

+The classification puts files under \code{checks/}, and files whose names end
+in \code{Checks} or \code{Audit}, in the second row. Physical lines include
+comments and blank lines. These are source-volume figures, not counts of
+independent mathematical arguments or kernel proof-term sizes. The supplied
+\code{scripts/audit_sources.py} reproduces the census, token counts, hashes,

+The two largest generated step files account for 6,567 lines:
+\src{SplitCircuitSteps59}{ has 3,445, and }
+\src{GapCircuitSteps66}{ has 3,122.}
+They specialize existing generic evaluation theorems. Their size is relevant
+to emitted code, build granularity, and review ergonomics, but should not be
+reported as thousands of independently maintained proofs.
+
+After comments and strings are masked, the active source census finds no
+\code{sorry}, \code{axiom}, or \code{native_decide} tokens. This lexical result
+is not an audit of imported axioms. Endpoint axiom checks remain necessary.
+
+\subsection{Preserve the existing mathematical contract}
+
+The current formalization plan distinguishes older checked endpoints from
+the newer literal polynomial, native decoding, and internal-ZFC composition
+work. The README and \code{LEAN_EQUIVALENCE_PLAN.md} explicitly retain open
+links. A refactoring must preserve these distinctions; shortening a conditional
+lemma is not completion of the whole consistency equivalence.\cite{readme,plan}
+
+In particular, preserve the witness domain, the literal coefficient data,
+the exact source syntax, the representation witness count, and the dependence
+on every input coordinate. Preserve raw-input soundness for the proof checker.
+In object-model arguments, preserve quantification over a model's entire
+natural-number object rather than silently restricting to externally standard
+numerals.
+
+\subsection{Use several measures of success}
+
+Record hand-maintained proof structure, generated source, declaration count,
+source bytes, elaboration time, peak memory, and endpoint axioms separately.
+A short line containing 36 rewrite lemmas can be more burdensome than several
+well-named local facts. A three-line \code{decide} proof can be expensive to
+replay. A new general theorem can be an architectural improvement even if its
+first clients do not amortize the helper's source length.

+\section{Move renaming out of expression evaluation}

+\src{Representation}{ already provides \code{Expr.eval_rename}.}
+However, \code{Rep.reindex}, both sides of \code{Rep.conjunction}, and both
+sides of \code{Rep.disjunction} repeat the same assignment comparison:
+rewrite expression renaming, apply congruence, prove function equality, and
+split a sum index.

+The useful common law is
+\[
+ \operatorname{natAssignment}(v,w)\circ\operatorname{Sum.map}(f,g)
+ =\operatorname{natAssignment}(v\circ f,w\circ g).
+\]
+It gives the semantic rule:
+
+\begin{Lean}
+theorem eval_rename_natAssignment
+    (e : Expr (σ ⊕ α)) (f : σ → τ) (g : α → β)
+    (v : τ → Nat) (w : β → Nat) :
+    (e.rename (Sum.map f g)).eval (natAssignment v w) =
+      e.eval (natAssignment (v ∘ f) (w ∘ g)) := by
+  rw [Expr.eval_rename, natAssignment_comp_sumMap]
+\end{Lean}
+
+The assignment lemma itself is proved by \code{funext i; cases i <;> rfl}.
+The left and right witness layouts, using \code{Fin.castAdd} and
+\code{Fin.natAdd}, become instances. The supplied
+\code{AssignmentTransport.lean} contains the general law and both instances.

+Orient simplification toward removing a renaming from the expression evaluator
+and putting it in the assignment. Do not install both directions as simp rules.
+Keep these rules local or in a small named collection until their effect on
+other evaluators is clear. Coordinate constructors should expose their semantic
+interface before the larger arithmetic expression is normalized.

+This preserves executable representation data. In particular, replacing a
+\code{Rep} constructor with an existentially chosen representation would lose
+the point of the current design: \code{Rep} carries a specific expression
+and finite witness count in \code{Type}. The desired refactor changes proof
+fields while preserving those supplied data.

+\section{Replace half-radix case analysis with one identity}
+\label{sec:radix}
+
+\src{NativeCyclicRotation}{ defines a shifted digit by}
+\[
+ D_{\rho,s}(a,b)=(sa\bmod\rho)+\left\lfloor\frac{sb}{\rho}\right\rfloor,
+\]
+where $a=c(k)$ and $b=c(k-1)$. Its half-radix bounds analyze the possible
+small digits separately. The arithmetic has a simpler normal form.
+
+\begin{proposition}
+For natural numbers $s,a,b$ with $s>0$,
+\[
+ D_{2s,s}(a,b)=s(a\bmod2)+\lfloor b/2\rfloor.
+\]
+Consequently, if $b\le3$, then $D_{2s,s}(a,b)\le s+1$.
+If also $s\equiv0\pmod2$, then
+\[
+ D_{2s,s}(a,b)\bmod2=\lfloor b/2\rfloor.
+\]
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Multiplication by $s$ commutes with remainder modulo $2s$, and positive
+multiplicative cancellation gives $\lfloor sb/(2s)\rfloor=\lfloor b/2\rfloor$.
+Now $a\bmod2\le1$ and $b\le3$ imply $\lfloor b/2\rfloor\le1$.
+When $s$ is even, the first summand has even parity and the second is less
+than 2, giving the final equality.
+\end{proof}
+
+The exact Lean proof of the identity is short:
+
+\begin{Lean}
+theorem step_eq (s a b : Nat) (hs : 0 < s) :
+    step s a b = s * (a % 2) + b / 2 := by
+  unfold step
+  rw [Nat.mul_comm 2 s, Nat.mul_mod_mul_left,
+    Nat.mul_div_mul_left _ _ hs]
+\end{Lean}
+
+\code{HalfRadix.lean} checks the identity, bound, and parity statement using
+only Lean core and its proof-producing \code{omega} tactic. This is stronger
+than the existing local bound: the current digit $a$ needs no upper bound;
+only the predecessor $b$ is constrained. Existing public statements can remain
+as corollaries, so callers need not change.
+
+The distinction between generality and integration matters. This file proves
+the scalar arithmetic used by the repository definition. It does not replay
+the entire cyclic-rotation dependency chain or the later phase argument.
+Specialization to $s=2^{88}$ is routine, but should still be compiled in the
+original module before committing the replacement.
+

+\subsection{A stronger abstraction: a finite majorant certificate}
+
+The envelope has the nonnegative monomial basis
+\[
+ m=(\beta^2,\ M_F\beta,\ M_C,\ M_F,\ \beta,\ K\beta,\ K,\ 1)
+\]
+with weight vector $b=(2,2,1,1,2,1,1,8)$. Each coefficient branch is an integer
+linear combination $\sum_i a_i m_i$ with small integer $a_i$. Prove once that
+$m_i\ge0$ and $|a_i|\le b_i$ imply
+\[
+ \left|\sum_i a_i m_i\right|\le\sum_i |a_i|m_i
+ \le\sum_i b_i m_i.
+\]
+Then each concrete branch needs only a finite small-integer vector certificate.
+This can serve multiple coefficient packages and reduces repeated arithmetic
+reasoning more deeply than a compact tactic script. It is a proposed design,
+not an implemented result. The basis must retain the existing linear dependence
+on the large transport port $K$; an easier bound quadratic in $K$ would not
+preserve the downstream published scale.

+\section{Share scanner proofs at the correct semantic boundary}
+\label{sec:scanners}
+
+Five families repeat the same iteration facts:
+\src{AnnotatedRenameScan}{, }
+\src{AnnotatedBoundScan}{, }
+\src{AnnotatedLineScan}{, }
+\src{AnnotatedContext}{, and }
+\src{AnnotatedAxiomContext}{.}

+\code{Function.iterate} facts. A one-time bridge from the current
+\code{Nat.rec} convention can reuse them.\cite{mathlib-iterate}

+The larger repetition is the simulation of an encoded list by a numeric
+scanner. The following interface isolates it without replacing the supplied
+numeric program:
+
+\begin{Lean}
+structure Encoding (next : A → H → Option H) (step : S → S) where
+  state : List A → H → S
+  reject : S
+  reject_fixed : step reject = reject
+  done_fixed : ∀ h, step (state [] h) = state [] h
+  cons_step : ∀ row rows h,
+    step (state (row :: rows) h) =
+      match next row h with
+      | none => reject
+      | some h' => state rows h'
+\end{Lean}
+
+For the associated typed list executor \code{run}, the common theorem is:
+\[
+ |\mathit{rows}|\le f\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
+ \operatorname{iterate}(\mathit{step},f,
+     \mathit{state}(\mathit{rows},h))
+ =\operatorname{result}(\operatorname{run}(\mathit{rows},h)).
+\]
+The proof is induction on the list. At an empty list, the state is fixed;
+at a rejected row, rejection is fixed; at a successful row, consume one unit
+of fuel and apply the induction hypothesis. The prelude-only
+\code{ScannerCore.lean} checks this theorem and the accompanying invariant
+lemmas without additional axioms.

+The same distinction applies to finished states. The generic interface does

+row. The proof is an instance of a very small general fact.
+
+For a row family $r:I\to R$ and distinct indices $d,s$, define
+\[
+ (\operatorname{addAt}_{d,s}r)(k)=
+ \begin{cases}r(d)+r(s)&k=d,\\r(k)&k\ne d.\end{cases}
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ (\forall k,\ (\operatorname{addAt}_{d,s}r)(k)=0)
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (\forall k,\ r(k)=0).
+\]
+The forward direction first reads the unchanged source row $s$, obtaining
+$r(s)=0$, and then reads the destination row. No cancellation or inverse
+operation is necessary: a type with addition and the usual zero laws suffices.
+Distinctness of $d$ and $s$ is essential to this argument.
+
+\code{RowOperations.lean} checks this generic theorem and the corresponding
+fact for a surjective reindexing. The intended concrete refactoring expresses
+the transformed family as two elementary row additions, then invokes this
+theorem twice. The final reordering uses the existing
+\code{rowOrder_surjective}. The equality between the actual transformed
+syntax and those elementary operations remains to be established; it is the
+finite binding certificate, not an assumption to omit.
+
+This is preferable to introducing a full matrix library solely for two row
+additions. If later transformations include arbitrary invertible linear
+combinations, a matrix-based zero-set preservation theorem becomes appropriate.
+The current case supports a much smaller interface.
+
+\section{Simplify object-model proof transport without changing strength}
+\label{sec:object}
+
+The exact expression \code{completeness_inf_context ZFCax_s []} appears
+26 times across 17 \code{Object*.lean} files. The repeated proof shell obtains
+a model, extracts its ZF axioms, establishes validity of the sealed formula,
+and invokes completeness. Good targets include
+\src{ObjectNaturalExpression}{, }
+\src{ObjectCodeClosure}{, }
+\src{ObjectCodeBound}{, }
+\src{ObjectPairingGraph}{, and }
+\src{ObjectResidualSquares}{.}
+
+Prove a wrapper taking the same model-universe quantification and semantic
+validity hypothesis and returning the same sealed \code{BProv} conclusion.
+Then every caller can focus on its specific arithmetic or coding argument.
+This theorem should be derived from the current completeness and sealing
+lemmas; it adds no axiom and gives no license to transfer arbitrary external
+theorems about standard naturals into ZFC.
+
+\subsection{An especially small arity-polymorphism improvement}
+
+In \src{ObjectQuarticCompiler}{, \code{zfc_proves_compiler} proves two versions
+of the same environment-invariance fact.}
+Its local helper is tied to the input arity $m$, so the compiled expression's
+different arity needs a separate \code{closedTarget} proof. Generalize
+
+\begin{Lean}
+have closed (f : Expr (Fin m)) : ... := ...
+\end{Lean}
+
+to
+
+\begin{Lean}
+have closed {n : Nat} (f : Expr (Fin n)) : ... := ...
+\end{Lean}
+
+and use it at both arities. The body already uses the arity-independent
+\code{sat_noZeroForm_iff} and \code{Sat_sentence_inv}. This proposed edit is
+source-inspected; the package does not claim a fresh build of its full
+object-theory dependency chain.
+
+\subsection{Build on the algebraic interfaces already present}
+
+The project already has \code{ObjectOmegaSemiring},
+\code{ObjectNaturalOrder}, \code{GatesSemiring}, and \code{QuarticSemiring}.
+The next step is to share model-independent finite-index and renaming facts
+between their callers. For example, conjunction of row families has the same
+index argument in \code{ObjectQuadraticSystem} and
+\code{QuadraticRegisterComposition}.
+
+Two constraints affect the design. First, directly importing
+\code{ObjectNaturalOrderedSemiring} into \code{ObjectResidualSquares} would
+create a cycle through \code{ObjectNaturalDiscrete}. Extract lower-level
+algebraic lemmas with only the needed assumptions or deliberately reorder the
+modules. Second, \code{ObjectNaturalExpression.evalRel_unique} currently does
+not assume every input lies in omega. A replacement proof that requires all
+inputs to be natural would weaken that theorem. Totality and uniqueness need
+not use exactly the same abstraction.
+
+\section{Improve the current-window API where coherence already exists}
+
+\src{CurrentPolynomialWindow2011}{ already contains a substantial
+\code{Facts} structure tying one source assignment, one window length,
+one Boolean word, one carry function, and one digit function together.}
+That design should be reused. The proposed improvement is to expose smaller
+proved views and derived quantities, not to introduce a competing record.
+
+Examples include a named temporal-shift expression, a view containing the
+four carry/mask facts needed by a local decoding lemma, and named fields for
+the source-coordinate transport. Construct \code{Facts} using named fields
+instead of a long positional tuple when this helps future edits. The latter
+does not necessarily shorten source, but makes an added field easier to audit.
+
+\src{CurrentDecodedWindow2011}{ correctly derives count and phase from the
+same arithmetic facts before invoking the cell decoder.}
+Keep that order. A ``simplified'' cell interface that assumes occupation or
+phase before the relevant polynomial theorem supplies them would make the
+composition circular. In particular, the decoded-cell alternatives still allow
+empty cells; the new interface must not quietly assume that every cell selects
+a tile.
+
+At the arithmetic boundary, derive reusable conversion facts once. Natural
+subtraction is truncated, integer subtraction is not, and \code{ZMod} values
+are representatives modulo the full window length. An unconditional rewrite
+between these interpretations is usually wrong. Good helper statements carry
+the exact positivity or range premise that makes the conversion valid.
+Then use \code{omega} for the remaining linear natural-number arithmetic and
+\code{ring} for equalities after entering the ring domain.
+
+This keeps representation changes separate from mathematical content. It is
+also more robust than adding long lists of low-level cast and subtraction
+lemmas to every downstream \code{simp} call.
+
+One especially local example is congruence weakening. The result
+\code{CurrentClause2011.reflected_weight_mod} works modulo 2048;
+\code{CurrentEarlyPadding2011.reflected_mod_sixteen} repeats the same
+selector/nonselector analysis modulo 16. The latter should follow through
+\code{Nat.ModEq.of_dvd}, since $16\mid2048$. The early-padding module already
+imports the clause module. The two local selector functions have the same
+defining equations; their definitional identification or a shared definition
+must be checked. This is a source-inspected one-line-wrapper opportunity,
+not a replayed project edit.
+
+\section{Finite checking and generated proof design}
+
+The desired trust boundary is ordinary Lean proof checking. A generator may
+produce a finite table, a reference map, or a proposed algebraic certificate;
+Lean must verify the assertion that table is used to justify. Keep certificate
+data independent of the conclusion and preserve the current endpoint axiom
+audits.
+
+Several practical experiments are worthwhile:
+
+\begin{enumerate}
+\item \textbf{Split large closed checks into stable pieces.} Compare a single
+\code{decide} over a large nested finite predicate with a small indexed family
+of checks or a partitioned certificate. This may change resource use, but
+neither short source nor many small cases guarantees faster replay.
+\item \textbf{Reduce data selection before symbolic branching.} For row
+coefficient proofs, choose the finite row and simplify vector indexing before
+splitting conditionals. Otherwise a tactic may inspect branches belonging to
+unselected rows.
+\item \textbf{Keep high-level cuts explicit.} Do not make large register
+expansion lemmas global simp rules. Use local lists of established semantic
+facts and prove small ring identities at the resulting boundaries.
+\item \textbf{Edit the generator with its output.} Check byte-for-byte
+regeneration and compile the emitted proof. A passing generator test alone
+does not certify its mathematical output.
+\item \textbf{Retain compatibility wrappers when useful.} Public theorem
+names referenced by checks can remain as thin corollaries of a generic proof.
+Private wrappers can be removed after confirming their scope.
+\end{enumerate}
+
+These recommendations do not require replacing kernel reduction with
+\code{native_decide}. The current source avoids that tactic. A tactic or
+certificate generator should emit ordinary checked proof terms if the existing
+axiom footprint is to be retained. Changes to trust assumptions should be
+explicit design decisions, not incidental source-shortening techniques.
+
+\section{Verification results and limitations}
+\label{sec:validation}
+
+The archive separates three kinds of evidence: kernel checks of new general
+lemmas, exact source-data checks, and source-inspected proposals. A success in
+one category is not promoted to another.
+
+\begin{longtable}{p{0.35\textwidth}p{0.57\textwidth}}
+\toprule
+Artifact & Verified scope\\
+\midrule
+\endhead
+\code{ScannerCore.lean} and audit & Seven general scanner/iteration theorems
+compiled with Lean 4.32.0; all seven have empty axiom lists. Concrete scanner
+adapters are not yet integrated.\\
+\code{LookupCleanup.lean} & Both exact polymorphic replacement statements
+compiled; each uses only \code{propext}. Seven-edit patch applies to the pinned
+source; the five full modified modules were not rebuilt.\\
+\code{HalfRadix.lean} & Identity, bound, and parity theorems compiled. Axiom
+lists use only \code{propext} and, for the bound/parity proofs, \code{Quot.sound}.\\
+\code{AssignmentTransportCore.lean} & Polymorphic \code{Sum.elim}/\code{Sum.map}
+composition law compiled; its axiom list is \code{Quot.sound}. Repository-specific
+clients are separate candidates.\\
+\code{RowOperations.lean} & Elementary row-addition and surjective-reindexing
+theorems compiled. The concrete Split certificate binding is still proposed.\\
+\code{inspect_shared_tail.py} & Pinned JSON inputs and regeneration of both
+circuit/step families checked; 99-node reference-renamed equality passes.
+No common-block Lean semantic theorem is claimed.\\
+\code{split-register-cuts.patch} & Generator/output source transformation and
+unchanged theorem statements checked. Full generated-module replay remains
+required.\\
+Coefficient-row candidates & Last combined isolated-definition replay timed
+out after 90 seconds without diagnostics. The 549- and 303-line deletions are
+unverified candidates. Exact scope is recorded in
+\code{evidence/arithmetic/verification.json}.\\
+Other circuit/model prototypes & Source-grounded proposals; their file-specific
+status is recorded in \code{evidence/verification.json}. No whole-project
+refactoring or build is claimed.\\
+\bottomrule
+\end{longtable}
+
+\subsection{Resource-limited checks are not performance measurements}
+
+The pinned compiler and dependency cache were obtained, and several upstream
+project modules were built. An attempted targeted build later exited with
+code 137 while building \code{SelectiveCertificate52}. The environment's shared
+memory limit was 8 GiB and was under concurrent load. This is a resource-limited
+replay, not evidence that the original proof is mathematically wrong or that
+this particular certificate intrinsically requires more than 8 GiB.
+
+A repository-dependent assignment-transport example also aborted under an
+explicit 1 GiB Lean cap before any theorem diagnostic. An import-only probe
+for the arithmetic harness exceeded that cap as well. These observations do
+not establish a relative cost between the proposed and original proofs.
+No timing speedup or memory reduction is claimed in this report.
+
+\subsection{What the delivered evidence does establish}
+
+The elementary general lemmas are actual checked Lean code. The source census
+and fixed-data comparisons are reproducible. The patches and prototypes give
+specific theorem-level changes that can be reviewed in the original project.
+The package also identifies where full imported-module replay, concrete adapter
+proofs, and endpoint audits remain necessary before integration.
+
+\section{A concrete migration plan}
+
+\textbf{First change set: library reuse and local algebra.}
+Apply the lookup patch and run the affected checks. Add the half-radix identity
+and retain the original bound/parity names as corollaries. Add the assignment
+transport rule at the existing representation layer. Generalize the local
+arity-polymorphic helper in \code{ObjectQuarticCompiler}. These changes have
+small semantic surfaces and can be reviewed separately.
+
+\textbf{Second change set: repeated finite proofs.}
+Validate the row-envelope replacement against the original imports; preserve
+the exact coefficient definition and the public theorem statements. Replace
+the coefficient-mapping family with one naturality proof. Bind the actual
+Split row transformation to the small row-operation interface. Promote the
+existing shared sum-of-squares and cost lemmas. Compile downstream public
+theorems after each step.
+
+\textbf{Third change set: shared scanner and circuit infrastructure.}
+Integrate the scanner interface first in RenameScan and BoundScan, where the
+common shape is clearest, then LineScan and AxiomContext. Keep all-code
+soundness and typed completeness separate. For the circuit family, apply the
+semantic-cut generator change and then extract the 99-node tail with exact
+parent-list binding theorems. Generalize positive/natural translation after
+the block reference interface has settled.
+
+At each step compare exact signatures, executable program data, witness counts,
+and endpoint axioms. For generated code, run its reproducibility check. Measure
+resource use on the same machine under comparable load only after the relevant
+modules replay successfully. Report net size after counting new helper modules,
+adapters, and compatibility wrappers.
+
+\appendix
+\section{Archive guide and reproduction}
+
+The principal files are \code{report.tex} and \code{report.pdf}.
+\code{README.txt} gives the file inventory and runnable commands.
+\code{lean/checked/} contains checked small examples; \code{lean/candidates/}

+xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error report.tex

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Reproduce descriptive metrics for the pinned active Lean source tree.
+
+Usage: python3 audit_sources.py /path/to/ProveIt /path/to/output
+Only Computability/DiophantineConsistency/Lean is included. Historical
+manuscript copies and generated build products are deliberately excluded.
+Declaration spans are lexical estimates, not Lean AST or proof-term sizes.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+import argparse
+import collections
+import csv
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import subprocess
+
+PIN = "60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c"
+ROOT = Path("Computability/DiophantineConsistency/Lean")
+TACTICS = ["simp", "simpa", "simp_all", "omega", "ring", "ring_nf",
+           "nlinarith", "linarith", "norm_num", "decide", "native_decide",
+           "aesop", "funext", "fin_cases", "rcases", "congr", "subst"]
+
+
+def strip_comments_and_strings(s: str) -> str:
+    """Mask nested Lean comments and strings, preserving line positions."""
+    out, i, depth = [], 0, 0
+    while i < len(s):
+        if depth:
+            if s.startswith("/-", i):
+                depth += 1; out.extend("  "); i += 2
+            elif s.startswith("-/", i):
+                depth -= 1; out.extend("  "); i += 2
+            else:
+                out.append("\n" if s[i] == "\n" else " "); i += 1
+        elif s.startswith("/-", i):
+            depth = 1; out.extend("  "); i += 2
+        elif s.startswith("--", i):
+            j = s.find("\n", i)
+            if j == -1: j = len(s)
+            out.extend(" " * (j - i)); i = j
+        elif s[i] == '"':
+            out.append(" "); i += 1
+            while i < len(s):
+                c = s[i]; out.append("\n" if c == "\n" else " "); i += 1
+                if c == "\\" and i < len(s):
+                    out.append("\n" if s[i] == "\n" else " "); i += 1
+                elif c == '"': break
+        else:
+            out.append(s[i]); i += 1
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+def write_csv(path: Path, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
+    if not rows: return
+    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
+        writer.writeheader(); writer.writerows(rows)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    ap.add_argument("repository", type=Path)
+    ap.add_argument("output", type=Path)
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    commit = subprocess.check_output(
+        ["git", "-C", str(args.repository), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip()
+    files, declarations, edges = [], [], []
+    counts = collections.Counter()
+    decl_pattern = re.compile(
+        r"^(?:@\[[^\n]*\]\s*)?(?:(?:private|protected|noncomputable|unsafe)\s+)*"
+        r"(theorem|lemma|def|abbrev|structure|inductive|instance)\s+([^\s(:{]+)", re.M)
+    for p in sorted((args.repository / ROOT).rglob("*.lean")):
+        raw = p.read_bytes(); s = raw.decode("utf-8"); clean = strip_comments_and_strings(s)
+        rel = str(p.relative_to(args.repository))
+        check = "checks" in p.relative_to(args.repository / ROOT).parts or p.stem.endswith(("Checks", "Audit"))
+        generated = bool(re.search(r"\bgenerated\b", s[:2500], re.I))
+        local = {t: len(re.findall(r"\b" + t + r"\b", clean)) for t in TACTICS}
+        row = dict(path=rel, category="check/audit" if check else "library/aggregate",
+                   header_mentions_generated=generated, physical_lines=len(s.splitlines()),
+                   nonblank_code_lines=sum(bool(x.strip()) for x in clean.splitlines()),
+                   utf8_bytes=len(raw), sha256=hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(), **local)
+        files.append(row)
+        if not check: counts.update(local)
+        matches = list(decl_pattern.finditer(clean))
+        for j, m in enumerate(matches):
+            start = clean.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
+            endpos = matches[j+1].start() if j+1 < len(matches) else len(clean)
+            end = clean.count("\n", 0, endpos) + 1
+            declarations.append(dict(path=rel, kind=m[1], name=m[2], start_line=start,
+                                     next_declaration_line=end, estimated_span_lines=end-start,
+                                     check_or_audit=check))
+        for target in re.findall(r"^import\s+(\S+)", clean, re.M):
+            edges.append(dict(source=rel, imported_module=target))
+    library = [r for r in files if r["category"] == "library/aggregate"]
+    trust = collections.Counter()
+    for row in files:
+        s = strip_comments_and_strings((args.repository / row["path"]).read_text())
+        trust.update(re.findall(r"\b(?:sorry|axiom|native_decide)\b", s))
+    report = dict(commit=commit, expected_commit=PIN, commit_matches=commit == PIN,
+                  scope=str(ROOT), files=len(files), physical_lines=sum(r["physical_lines"] for r in files),
+                  library_or_aggregate_files=len(library),
+                  library_or_aggregate_lines=sum(r["physical_lines"] for r in library),
+                  check_or_audit_files=len(files)-len(library),
+                  check_or_audit_lines=sum(r["physical_lines"] for r in files if r not in library),
+                  lexical_tactic_counts_library=dict(counts), lexical_trust_tokens_all=dict(trust),
+                  largest_library_files=sorted(library, key=lambda r:r["physical_lines"], reverse=True)[:25],
+                  caveats=["Line counts include comments and blanks unless labeled nonblank_code_lines.",
+                           "Tactic counts are lexical token counts after comment/string masking.",
+                           "The token decide includes bound proofs in data, not only theorem proofs.",
+                           "Header detection of generated files is a heuristic, not an exhaustive classification.",
+                           "Declaration spans include following commands/comments and are only prioritization hints.",
+                           "No full repository build or axiom audit is implied by these source metrics."])
+    (args.output / "source_metrics.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
+    write_csv(args.output / "source_files.csv", files)
+    write_csv(args.output / "declaration_spans.csv", sorted(declarations, key=lambda r:r["estimated_span_lines"], reverse=True))
+    write_csv(args.output / "imports.csv", edges)
+    print(json.dumps({k:report[k] for k in ["commit", "files", "physical_lines", "library_or_aggregate_files",
+                                          "library_or_aggregate_lines", "check_or_audit_files", "check_or_audit_lines",
+                                          "lexical_trust_tokens_all"]}, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Replay the package's small checked Lean examples without modifying ProveIt.
+
+--repo optionally adds the repository's already-built Mathlib environment and
+checks RowOperations. No dependency download, Lake update, or repository edit
+is performed. Larger candidates are deliberately not represented as checked.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import time
+
+PIN = "60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c"
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    ap.add_argument("--lean", default=shutil.which("lean") or "lean")
+    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--repo", type=Path)
+    ap.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=180)
+    ap.add_argument("--memory-mb", type=int, default=2048)
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+    package = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+    source = package / "lean" / "checked"
+    output = args.out.resolve()
+    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    oleans = output / "olean"
+    oleans.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    version = subprocess.check_output([args.lean, "--version"], text=True).strip()
+    if "version 4.32.0," not in version:
+        raise SystemExit(f"Expected Lean 4.32.0, found: {version}")
+    paths = [str(oleans)]
+    if args.repo:
+        repo = args.repo.resolve()
+        commit = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(repo), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip()
+        if commit != PIN:
+            raise SystemExit(f"Expected repository commit {PIN}, found {commit}")
+        paths.append(str(repo / ".lake/build/lib/lean"))
+        paths.extend(str(p) for p in sorted((repo / ".lake/packages").glob("*/.lake/build/lib/lean")))
+    env = dict(os.environ)
+    env["LEAN_PATH"] = os.pathsep.join(paths)

+        if name == "ScannerCore":

+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
+            code, timed_out = None, True

+                   elapsed_seconds=round(time.monotonic()-start, 3),
+                   status="PASS" if code == 0 else "NOT_VERIFIED")
+        results.append(row)
+        print(f"{name}: {row['status']}", flush=True)
+        if code != 0: break
+    report = dict(lean_version=version, results=results,
+                  note="Elapsed time is a replay receipt, not a controlled benchmark.")
+    (output / "verification.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2)+"\n")
+    if len(results) != len(jobs) or any(r["exit_code"] != 0 for r in results):
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+
+sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
+
+BASE = "60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c"
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    repo = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
+    commit = subprocess.check_output(
+        ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=repo, text=True
+    ).strip()
+    if commit != BASE:
+        raise SystemExit(f"Expected commit {BASE}, found {commit}")
+    tools = repo / "Computability/DiophantineConsistency/tools"
+
+    def load(name):
+        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, tools / (name + ".py"))
+        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+        return module
+
+    split_generator = load("generate_split_recipe_steps59")
+    gap_generator = load("generate_gap_recipe_steps66")
+    lean_dir = repo / "Computability/DiophantineConsistency/Lean/DiophantineConsistency"
+    generated_sources = {
+        "SplitCircuit59.lean": split_generator.g.render(),
+        "GapCircuit66.lean": gap_generator.g.render(),
+        "SplitCircuitSteps59.lean": split_generator.render(),
+        "GapCircuitSteps66.lean": gap_generator.render(),
+    }
+    source_matches = {
+        name: (lean_dir / name).read_text() == source
+        for name, source in generated_sources.items()
+    }
+    if not all(source_matches.values()):
+        raise SystemExit(f"Generated sources differ: {source_matches}")
+    split = split_generator.nodes[416:]
+    gap = gap_generator.nodes[385:]
+    remap = {i: i for i in range(18)} | {21: 87, 409: 378, 414: 383, 415: 384}
+    normalized = []
+    external = set()
+    for node in split:
+        item = dict(node)
+        for key in ("left", "right"):
+            if key in item:
+                index = item[key]
+                if index < 416:
+                    external.add(index)
+                item[key] = index - 31 if index >= 416 else remap[index]
+        normalized.append(item)
+    equal = normalized == gap
+    result = {
+        "base_commit": commit,
+        "split_suffix_start": 416,
+        "gap_suffix_start": 385,
+        "split_suffix_nodes": len(split),
+        "gap_suffix_nodes": len(gap),
+        "exact_suffix_equality_after_remap": equal,
+        "generated_sources_match": source_matches,
+        "suffix_node_kinds": dict(Counter(n["kind"] for n in split)),
+        "source_json_sha256": {
+            "split_natural": split_generator.g.PINS["natural"],
+            "gap_natural": gap_generator.g.PINS["natural"],
+        },
+        "boundary_map": {str(i): remap[i] for i in sorted(external)},
+        "local_map": "j -> j - 31 for j >= 416",
+        "verification": "Python source-data equality; not a Lean theorem",
+    }
+    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
+    if not equal:
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic
+import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
+
+/-!
+Dependency-light arithmetic interfaces suggested by the current and legacy
+DiophantineConsistency proofs. This file deliberately does not import any
+project theorem: the generalized lemmas can sit below the current modules.
+-/
+
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.ArithmeticRefactors
+
+/- Both CurrentClause2011 and CurrentReflectedGeometry2011 prove the two
+   following identities separately at L = 2011. -/
+theorem addition_residue {N L : ℕ} [NeZero (N * L)]
+    (b : ZMod (N * L)) (e : ℕ) :
+    (b + (e : ZMod (N * L))).val % L = (b.val + e) % L := by
+  have hh : (((b + (e : ZMod (N * L))).val : ℕ) : ZMod (N * L)) =
+      ((b.val + e : ℕ) : ZMod (N * L)) := by
+    simp only [Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
+  exact ((ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff _ _ _).mp hh).of_dvd ⟨N, by ring⟩
+
+theorem subtraction_residue {N L : ℕ} [NeZero (N * L)]
+    (k : ZMod (N * L)) (e : ℕ) :
+    ((k - (e : ZMod (N * L))).val + e) % L = k.val % L := by
+  have hh : (((k - (e : ZMod (N * L))).val + e : ℕ) : ZMod (N * L)) =
+      (k.val : ZMod (N * L)) := by
+    simp only [Nat.cast_add, ZMod.natCast_zmod_val, sub_add_cancel]
+  exact ((ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff _ _ _).mp hh).of_dvd ⟨N, by ring⟩
+
+/- A scaled half-radix digit has this exact form, regardless of any digit
+   bound. The two original four-valued proofs become corollaries. -/
+theorem scaled_div_mod (s x y : ℕ) (hs : 0 < s) :
+    s * x % (2 * s) + s * y / (2 * s) = s * (x % 2) + y / 2 := by
+  rw [mul_comm 2 s, Nat.mul_mod_mul_left, Nat.mul_div_mul_left _ _ hs]
+
+theorem scaled_half_bound (s x y : ℕ) (hs : 0 < s) (hy : y ≤ 3) :
+    s * x % (2 * s) + s * y / (2 * s) ≤ s + 1 := by
+  rw [scaled_div_mod s x y hs]
+  have hx : x % 2 ≤ 1 := by omega
+  have hy' : y / 2 ≤ 1 := by omega
+  have hm := Nat.mul_le_mul_left s hx
+  omega
+
+theorem scaled_half_parity (s x y : ℕ) (hs : 0 < s)
+    (heven : s % 2 = 0) (hy : y ≤ 3) :
+    (s * x % (2 * s) + s * y / (2 * s)) % 2 = y / 2 := by
+  rw [scaled_div_mod s x y hs, Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, heven]
+  have hy' : y / 2 < 2 := by omega
+  simp [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hy']
+
+#print axioms addition_residue
+#print axioms subtraction_residue
+#print axioms scaled_div_mod
+#print axioms scaled_half_bound
+#print axioms scaled_half_parity
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.ArithmeticRefactors

+import DiophantineConsistency.Representation
+
+/-!
+Small, additive proof-refactoring prototype for ProveIt commit
+60e9c5d620c6c387d932876cfa2d9376f64ea56c. The representation data are
+unchanged; only the correctness proofs use a shared naturality lemma.
+-/
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.ProofRefactor
+
+variable {σ τ α β : Type*}
+
+/-- Input and witness renaming commute with the natural-to-integer assignment. -/
+theorem natAssignment_comp_sumMap (v : τ → ℕ) (w : β → ℕ)
+    (f : σ → τ) (g : α → β) :
+    natAssignment v w ∘ Sum.map f g = natAssignment (v ∘ f) (w ∘ g) := by
+  funext i
+  cases i <;> rfl
+
+/-- One interface replaces repeated `congrArg`/`funext` proofs at call sites. -/
+theorem eval_rename_natAssignment (e : Expr (σ ⊕ α))
+    (f : σ → τ) (g : α → β) (v : τ → ℕ) (w : β → ℕ) :
+    (e.rename (Sum.map f g)).eval (natAssignment v w) =
+      e.eval (natAssignment (v ∘ f) (w ∘ g)) := by
+  rw [Expr.eval_rename, natAssignment_comp_sumMap]
+
+variable {P Q : (σ → ℕ) → Prop}
+
+/-- Reindexing needs only the shared naturality equation. -/
+def reindex (r : Rep σ P) (f : σ → τ) : Rep τ (fun v => P (v ∘ f)) where
+  witnessCount := r.witnessCount
+  expression := r.expression.rename (Sum.map f id)
+  correct v := by
+    simpa only [eval_rename_natAssignment, Function.comp_id] using r.correct (v ∘ f)
+
+/-- The same conjunction data, with all four block/assignment adapters shared. -/
+def conjunction (r : Rep σ P) (s : Rep σ Q) : Rep σ (fun v => P v ∧ Q v) := by
+  let left := r.expression.rename (Sum.map id (Fin.castAdd s.witnessCount))
+  let right := s.expression.rename (Sum.map id (Fin.natAdd r.witnessCount))
+  refine ⟨r.witnessCount + s.witnessCount, left * left + right * right, ?_⟩
+  intro v
+  simp only [left, right, Expr.eval_add, Expr.eval_mul, eval_rename_natAssignment,
+    Function.comp_id, mul_self_add_mul_self_eq_zero]
+  rw [r.correct, s.correct]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨⟨a, ha⟩, ⟨b, hb⟩⟩
+    refine ⟨Fin.addCases a b, ?_, ?_⟩
+    · simpa [Function.comp_def] using ha
+    · simpa [Function.comp_def] using hb
+  · rintro ⟨w, ha, hb⟩
+    exact ⟨⟨w ∘ Fin.castAdd s.witnessCount, ha⟩,
+      ⟨w ∘ Fin.natAdd r.witnessCount, hb⟩⟩
+
+/-- The same disjunction data; the unused witness block remains all zero. -/
+def disjunction (r : Rep σ P) (s : Rep σ Q) : Rep σ (fun v => P v ∨ Q v) := by
+  let left := r.expression.rename (Sum.map id (Fin.castAdd s.witnessCount))
+  let right := s.expression.rename (Sum.map id (Fin.natAdd r.witnessCount))
+  refine ⟨r.witnessCount + s.witnessCount, left * right, ?_⟩
+  intro v
+  simp only [left, right, Expr.eval_mul, eval_rename_natAssignment,
+    Function.comp_id, mul_eq_zero]
+  rw [r.correct, s.correct]
+  constructor
+  · rintro (⟨a, ha⟩ | ⟨b, hb⟩)
+    · refine ⟨Fin.addCases a (fun _ => 0), Or.inl ?_⟩
+      simpa [Function.comp_def] using ha
+    · refine ⟨Fin.addCases (fun _ => 0) b, Or.inr ?_⟩
+      simpa [Function.comp_def] using hb
+  · rintro ⟨w, ha | hb⟩
+    · exact Or.inl ⟨w ∘ Fin.castAdd s.witnessCount, ha⟩
+    · exact Or.inr ⟨w ∘ Fin.natAdd r.witnessCount, hb⟩
+
+/-- Data preservation includes both syntax and witness count. -/
+theorem reindex_eq (r : Rep σ P) (f : σ → τ) :
+    reindex r f = r.reindex f := by rfl
+
+theorem conjunction_eq (r : Rep σ P) (s : Rep σ Q) :
+    conjunction r s = r.conjunction s := by rfl
+
+theorem disjunction_eq (r : Rep σ P) (s : Rep σ Q) :
+    disjunction r s = r.disjunction s := by rfl
+
+#print axioms natAssignment_comp_sumMap
+#print axioms eval_rename_natAssignment
+#print axioms reindex
+#print axioms conjunction
+#print axioms disjunction
+#print axioms reindex_eq
+#print axioms conjunction_eq
+#print axioms disjunction_eq
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.ProofRefactor

+import Mathlib.Logic.Function.Iterate
+
+/-!
+Shared iteration facts for the five annotated numeric scanner families.
+The definition matches their existing Nat.rec implementation exactly.
+This is an additive, checked interface, not a replacement proof of any
+scanner's local checker soundness or primitive-recursive program realization.
+-/
+namespace DiophantineConsistency.ScannerCore
+
+universe u
+variable {S : Type u}
+
+def scan (step : S → S) (fuel : Nat) (initial : S) : S :=
+  fuel.rec initial (fun _ acc => step acc)
+
+@[simp] theorem scan_zero (step : S → S) (initial : S) :
+    scan step 0 initial = initial := rfl
+
+theorem scan_succ (step : S → S) (fuel : Nat) (initial : S) :
+    scan step (fuel + 1) initial = scan step fuel (step initial) := by
+  induction fuel with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | succ fuel ih => exact congrArg step ih
+
+theorem scan_fixed (step : S → S) {initial : S}
+    (h : step initial = initial) (fuel : Nat) :
+    scan step fuel initial = initial := by
+  induction fuel with
+  | zero => rfl
+  | succ fuel ih => exact (congrArg step ih).trans h
+
+theorem scan_invariant (step : S → S) (P : S → Prop)
+    (hstep : ∀ s, P s → P (step s)) {initial : S} (h : P initial)
+    (fuel : Nat) : P (scan step fuel initial) := by
+  induction fuel with
+  | zero => exact h
+  | succ fuel ih => exact hstep _ ih
+
+/-- A rejecting state can be included without assuming the input parses. -/
+theorem scan_reject_or_invariant (step : S → S) (reject : S)
+    (Good : S → Prop) (hreject : step reject = reject)
+    (hstep : ∀ s, Good s → step s = reject ∨ Good (step s))
+    {initial : S} (h : Good initial) (fuel : Nat) :
+    scan step fuel initial = reject ∨ Good (scan step fuel initial) := by
+  apply scan_invariant step (fun s => s = reject ∨ Good s) ?_ (Or.inr h) fuel
+  intro s hs
+  rcases hs with rfl | hs
+  · exact Or.inl hreject
+  · exact hstep s hs
+
+/-- The old raw recursion can use the shared lemma without a definition change. -/
+example (step : Nat → Nat) (hzero : step 0 = 0) (fuel : Nat) :
+    fuel.rec 0 (fun _ acc => step acc) = 0 :=
+  scan_fixed step hzero fuel
+
+#print axioms scan_succ
+#print axioms scan_fixed
+#print axioms scan_invariant
+#print axioms scan_reject_or_invariant
+
+end DiophantineConsistency.ScannerCore

+### Checked helpers
+
+- `ArithmeticRefactors.lean`: block residue identities and scaled div/mod lemmas.
+- `RotationRefactors.lean`: exact-signature alternatives for two original
+  half-radix rotation results; neither invokes the target theorem it replaces.
+- `ScannerCore.lean`: shared `Nat.rec` laws, fixed states and invariant preservation.
+- `FinitePushforward.lean`: weighted finite-fiber summation with collisions retained.
+- `RepresentationNaturality.lean`: shared assignment lemma, alternative constructors,
+  and `rfl` equality proofs against the originals.
+- `ListLookup.lean`: the pinned library API replacing a private lookup induction.
+
+The helper modules carry their own `#print axioms` commands. No `sorry`, new
+axiom, or native-evaluation shortcut was introduced. The scanner lemmas have
+empty axiom sets; other reported sets are subsets of `propext`,
+`Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
+
+## Reproduce the verification
+
+Use an existing checkout of the exact commit, with the pinned Lean toolchain
+and dependencies installed. The script does not install packages or build the
+entire repository. Its baseline module prerequisites are:
+
+```bash
+lake build DiophantineConsistency.Representation \
+  DiophantineConsistency.NativeQuadraticParent \
+  DiophantineConsistency.NativeCyclicRotation
+```
+
+Then run, replacing the two absolute example paths with your actual locations:
+
+```bash
+python3 /path/to/lean-proof-simplification-2026-10-26/scripts/verify.py \
+  /path/to/ProveIt
+```
+
+The script checks the repository commit, Lean version, and Mathlib commit;
+it assumes a clean checkout and unchanged built dependencies. It runs
+`git apply --check` on both diffs, compiles all six helpers,
+and compiles complete patched modules with axiom diagnostics appended. It
+records return codes, source/log hashes, elapsed observations and axiom sets.
+An unexpected axiom or failed command makes the replay fail. It leaves all
+repository source files unchanged.
+
+For an already configured separate Lake workspace whose project imports point
+at the same clean source snapshot and built dependencies, use
+`--lake-workspace /path/to/workspace`. Use
+`--lake /absolute/path/to/lake` when Lake is not on PATH. The optional
+`--output /path/to/evidence` chooses where the new replay logs and temporary
+Lean objects go. By default they are written to `validation/replay/`.
+
+The default module-level compile budget is unchanged except for the explicitly
+scoped option in the coefficient patch. Read the report for the distinction
+between source reduction and elaboration performance. Logged times were
+observed under concurrent load and are not speedup measurements.
+
+## Review or integrate the patches
+
+Each patch is independent and retains the original public names. Review the
+complete file in `patched/` alongside the corresponding diff. Apply it on a
+branch of the pinned checkout only after review, then replay the direct consumers
+appropriate to your integration target. The archive's checks do not claim to
+have rebuilt every downstream consumer.
+
+The representation patch preserves exact stored expression syntax and witness
+counts; the additive prototype supplies equality proofs by reflexivity. The
+coefficient patch preserves the original coefficient function, envelope and
+all exported theorem signatures. Removing repeated private proof trees does
+not change the underlying arithmetic construction.
+
+## Reproduce the source metrics
+
+```bash
+python3 scripts/audit_inventory.py /path/to/ProveIt --output /tmp/proof-inventory
+python3 scripts/audit_coefficient_refactor.py \
+  --repository /path/to/ProveIt \
+  --candidate patched/NativeCoefficientBounds.lean
+```
+
+The inventory is lexical, not a Lean elaboration or a transitive axiom audit.
+Its comment stripper handles nested Lean block comments. Declaration lengths
+are approximate lexical spans. The coefficient script separately compares
+public declaration headers and counts repeated proof text and coefficient
+expressions; this does not substitute for compilation.
+
+## Rebuild the PDF

+With a standard LaTeX installation containing `pdflatex`, Latin Modern,
+`microtype`, `listings`, `hyperref`, `xurl`, and the listed ordinary packages:
+
+```bash
+bash scripts/build_report.sh
+```

+The PDF was compiled from the supplied TeX and visually reviewed after rendering.
+Compiled Lean objects, downloaded dependencies, and the local compiler are not
+included in this small archive.
